channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: Travis Etienne rushed 14 times for 76 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Travis Etienne NO Running Back

The good news is that Etienne started the game for the Saints backfield and received 14-of-16 running back carries. He led the backfield with 21 total snaps as Audric Estime was a healthy scratch against the Bears. Etienne’s best run of the day was a 46-yard carry in the second quarter, where he was chased down and tackled inside the five-yard line. He got two more opportunities and got the ball to the one-yard line, but did not get the touchdown on that drive. Etienne’s lack of passing-game usage and Alvin Kamara’s involvement as a touchdown scorer caps Etienne’s ceiling for fantasy purposes. He belongs in the RB3 ranks for Week 12 against the Bengals.

item.title: Cade Otton caught 1-of-3 targets for eight yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
item.description:
Cade Otton TB Tight End

Otton popped up with a four-catch, eight-target game before the Bucs’ Week 10 bye. He was unable to build on that box score and all but disappeared today. Otton hasn’t topped five catches or 56 yards in a game this year. He has also been held without a touchdown through nearly three months of action. He’s barely even a TE2 for Week 12 against the Panthers.

item.title: George Pickens caught 7-of-10 targets for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens got off to a slow start this afternoon, seeming to not finish a route or two, but finished molten hot. He is now up to 18 catches for 247 yards and four touchdowns on 28 targets over the past two weeks. Ridiculous numbers, though somewhat sustainable in this narrow, explosive offense. For Thanksgiving Day he will be rematching with an Eagles defense he got for 4/57/1 last month. The Eagles have moved on to their No. 3 quarterback since then and traded a few key contributors. Even with all 32 teams active for Week 12, Pickens will remain in the low-end WR1 mix.

item.title: Kenneth Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions, adding four catches for 43 yards.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Bucs coach Todd Bowles told reporters on Monday that Gainwell could see more touches going forward to help keep Bucky Irving fresh. That couldn’t have been further from the truth today as Irving out-touched Gainwell 21-8. Gainwell did, however, post his second-best receiving line of the year. His only better game came two weeks ago, before Tampa’s bye, against the Bears. Gainwell might finally be developing a receptions-based floor, but a two-game sample can’t be taken as gospel. Gainwell will remain on the RB3/4 border when he takes on the Panthers next week.

item.title: Zavion Thomas caught 2-of-3 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding one carry for 30 yards.
item.description:
Zavion Thomas CHI Wide Receiver

Thomas was the subject of multiple explosive plays against the Saints. He saw just offensive 10 snaps, but Ben Johnson schemed up multiple plays to utilize the rookie receiver’s speed. A 40-yard reception in the third quarter and 30-yard rush in the second quarter highlighted a career-best day for Thomas. He is still not fantasy relevant, but his usage should be monitored as the Bears scheme up more plays for him.

item.title: Jaylen Warren had nine rushes for 28 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding two catches for one yard.
item.description:
Jaylen Warren PIT Running Back

Warren was snuffed out by a swarming Philadelphia defense that appeared committed to stopping the Pittsburgh rushing attack and forcing Aaron Rodgers to beat them (he did not). Warren ran 36 routes on the day to Rico Dowdle’s 16 routes, though it was Dowdle who led the backfield with five targets. Warren now has back-to-back down games in a collapsing Steelers offense. Things won’t get much easier in Week 12 against the Broncos.

item.title: Rico Dowdle had five rushes for 15 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding four catches for 19 yards.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Jaylen Warren, meanwhile, managed 29 yards on nine rushing attempts and caught one of his two targets. Dowdle got quite a lot of second half playing time, finishing the game with 16 pass routes to 36 routes for Warren. Dowdle is good for 7-10 touches per week in the low-octane Pittsburgh offense, making him a desperation flex option in deeper formats.

item.title: Kalif Raymond caught 1-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
item.description:
Kalif Raymond CHI Wide Receiver

Raymond was targeted four times, including an incomplete end zone target on fourth down in the first half. He caught one of his targets for 14 total yards, though he had the second-most wide receiver snaps on the team. Raymond is still involved as the starting outside receiver opposite Rome Odunze but has boom-or-bust WR5 viability at best heading into Week 12

item.title: Baker Mayfield completed 20-of-33 passes for 187 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ 31-21, Week 11 loss to the Lions.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield appeared to be unlikely to suit up for today’s game when the week started, but a pair of limited practices was enough to get him on the field today. Things got off to a scary start when he was crushed for a sack-fumble on his first dropback of the day. He would go on to take four sacks for a total loss of 33 yards. Somehow, Mayfield looked more than willing as a runner, adding 36 yards on six carries. It was ultimately a solid fantasy outing from Mayfield, assisted by a garbage-time touchdown to Ted Hurst. A date with the Panthers next week will keep Mayfield in the QB2 mix next week, but he’s far from the best streaming option available to most fantasy managers.

item.title: Mitchell Evans caught 5-of-5 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Mitchell Evans CAR Tight End

It was a career day for Evans, who posted career highs in targets, catches, and receiving yards, and scored his third touchdown as a pro in the first quarter. Evans caught a 23-yard touchdown pass from Bryce Young on a trick play that began with a direct snap to Jalen Coker, fighting through contact near the goal line to extend his arms across for the score. Evans’ production was impressive for a player who ran only 12 routes, per the early PFF data. That said, his low involvement should caution fantasy managers considering him as a streaming option after scouting the box score. Evans is best left on waivers heading into Week 12 against the Buccaneers.

item.title: Jalen Coker caught 4-of-7 targets for 47 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker’s biggest play of the game came on a 35-yard reception in the first quarter, which precluded a 23-yard touchdown pass to tight end Mitchell Evans on the following play. Coker would muster just 12 yards on his other three catches, as he was used primarily in the short and intermediate areas of the field. He took a hard hit from Ravens LB Roquan Smith late in the fourth quarter and was placed in the league’s concussion protocol. Assuming he remains in the league’s concussion protocol on Monday, Coker will need to clear several hurdles if he hopes to suit up for Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday Night Football.

Source: Sheena Quick

item.title: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Tetairoa McMillan CAR Wide Receiver

McMillan has scored twice in his last three games and led the Panthers in both targets and receptions in this one. His lone score came on a seven-yard pass from Bryce Young in the second quarter, but it could have been a much bigger day for McMillan were it not for an interception by Young in the third quarter. Young attempted to find McMillan again in the end zone in the third quarter, but a diving interception by Ravens CB T.J. Tampa ended any hopes of points for McMillan. McMillan has gone for 50-plus yards in three of his last four games and will be a strong WR2 in Week 12’s game against the Buccaneers.

item.title: CeeDee Lamb caught 11-of-12 targets for 132 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
item.description:
CeeDee Lamb DAL Wide Receiver

Lamb’s fifth 100-yard effort of the season and second in three weeks put him above 1,000 yards for the sixth consecutive season, good for a new Cowboys franchise record. Simply abusing overmatched Titans CB Cor’Dale Flott, it is barely an exaggeration to say Lamb was open at will against the Titans’ overmatched defense. The Eagles will be a slightly tougher Thanksgiving Day matchup, but not by much. Enjoy the holiday with your WR1.

item.title: Carnell Tate caught 2-of-5 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

Active for the first time since Week 7, the No. 4 overall pick caught a -1 yard pass in the first quarter before adding a 59-yard touchdown in the third. In between, he drew a 38-yard DPI in the end zone to set the Titans up at the one-yard line. On his score, Tate appeared to be down by contact near mid-field, but he realized he had not been touched and got up and sprinted to the end zone. Heady stuff, though we would have liked to see more targets. Tate thankfully avoided setbacks with his shoulder injury, and is now ready to slot into the WR24-30 range for a tough Week 12 matchup with the Jags. Tate would be a safer WR2 were it not a 32-team slate for the holiday week.

item.title: Jared Goff completed 20-of-28 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 31-21, Week 11 win over the Bucs.
item.description:
Jared Goff DET Quarterback

A long Bucs drive limited the Lions to one possession in the first quarter. Jake Bates missed his field goal try, resulting in a slow start for Detroit. They shook the rust off in the second quarter and cruised past the Bucs over the next three frames. Because Tampa’s offense didn’t put up much of a fight, Goff’s passing volume was limited once again. He hasn’t thrown for more than 32 passes in a game since Week 4. The good news for fantasy managers is that the Lions take on the Bears in what should be a Thanksgiving afternoon shootout next week. Goff topped 330 yards in both of his games against the Bears last year. He will be a top-half QB1 for Week 12.

item.title: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-4 targets for 45 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
item.description:
Rome Odunze CHI Wide Receiver

Odunze was involved in the intermediate area for the Bears, making a 19-yard grab on the first drive. He made a 16-yard catch later in the first half, getting tackled inside the five-yard line and setting up a touchdown. His four targets were tied for the most on the team, with Caleb Williams only attempting 23 passes against the Saints. Odunze’s downfield targets keep him in the FLEX conversation for fantasy purposes. He is in the WR3/FLEX ranks for Week 12 against the Lions.

item.title: Mark Andrews caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Mark Andrews BAL Tight End

Andrews’ disappointing performance comes a week after he caught eight targets for 82 yards in Jacoby Brissett’s debut with the Ravens. The Ravens worked to get all three tight ends involved in this one, as Andrews, Matthew Hibner, and Josh Cuevas combined to get eight targets, with Andrews and Cuevas both getting three looks. Andrews’ promising performance against the Chargers gave fantasy managers a reason to hope for more this week, especially with six teams on bye. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, it’s safe to say Andrews shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a desperation play on the road against the Texans.

item.title: Rashod Bateman caught 2-of-6 targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

Bateman’s touchdown pass came on a play from the wildcat that started with Derrick Henry receiving the snap. While Henry handed the ball off to Justice Hill, who then pitched to Jacoby Brissett, Bateman streaked down the field, leaving every member of the Panthers’ secondary in the dust as they attempted to dissect the trick play called by Ravens OC Declan Doyle. Brissett delivered a slightly underthrown ball to Bateman, but it proved inconsequential given the distance between Bateman and the nearest defender. The 26-year-old receiver hauled in the pass without any trouble and made his way into the end zone to give the Ravens an early 9-0 lead. Bateman would only catch one more pass the rest of the day, but his six targets now give him 11 in his two games with Brissett under center. While it’s hard to imagine Bateman having any reliable fantasy value this season, he could be worth a desperation dart throw in deeper leagues in Week 12 against the Texans.

item.title: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-11 targets for 97 yards in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

In two games with Jacoby Brissett, Flowers has caught 14-of-18 targets for 171 scoreless yards. This is great news for fantasy managers, who saw Flowers’ fantasy value in the tank when the duo of Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano led him to just six yards over a two-week stretch. Brissett’s arrival has been good news for Flowers, who ripped off two gains of 20-plus yards on the afternoon and led the Ravens in both targets and receiving yards. He will be a high-end WR2 next week against a Texans secondary that has proven vulnerable this season.

item.title: Luther Burden caught 2-of-3 targets for 10 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding one carry for three yards.
item.description:
Luther Burden CHI Wide Receiver

Burden had little involvement in a low-volume passing day for the Bears. He saw three of Caleb Williams’ 23 passing attempts on a day where no Bears pass-catcher had more than four targets. Rookie Zavion Thomas saw the splash plays on the day as Burden had short-yardage usage to pick up quick first downs out of the slot. The first half game script did not favor Burden, but given his elite production in recent weeks, he is back in the low-end WR2 ranks for a Thanksgiving day game against the Lions.

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 5-of-6 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

With only 28 attempts for Jared Goff, there simply wasn’t much receiving work to go around. St. Brown still led the Lions in targets alongside Sam LaPorta. Despite the quiet day, fantasy managers will be satisfied with St. Brown’s eighth touchdown of the year. He scored No. 8 on an easy strike over the middle of the field from 14 yards out. With a shootout versus the Bears scheduled for Thanksgiving, St. Brown is set for elite fantasy numbers in Week 12.

item.title: Cam Ward completed 21-of-30 passes for 248 yards and two touchdowns in the Titans’ 51-30, Week 11 loss to the Cowboys, adding two rushes for three yards and a third score.
item.description:
Cam Ward TEN Quarterback

Recalled from fantasy benches for streamer duties vs. the defense-less Cowboys, Ward had his first three-score game of the year. It was also his third straight multi-score effort after managing just one in first seven starts. No. 3 was a 12-yard garbage time connection with Calvin Ridley, but that description doesn’t really do it justice. Flushed from the pocket and seemingly running out of bounds, Ward instead made like prime Aaron Rodgers and threw the ball across his body, across the middle of the field into Ridley’s arms like it was a loaf of bread. It was the most impressive play of his young NFL career, and an exclamation point on his recent improved play. Today was a soft matchup, but that was not the case for the Jaguars in Week 10, with whom Ward must now rematch in Week 12. Despite his hot streak, Ward will find himself outside the top 20 for Thanksgiving week because of his tough setup and all 32 teams being active for the holiday slate.

item.title: The Baltimore Banner’s Giana Han reports Derrick Henry cleared concussion protocol after Week 11’s loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Derrick Henry BAL Running Back

Henry didn’t return to the field after exiting in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a concussion, but it was reportedly shortly after that he cleared the league’s concussion protocol. Henry rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in Sunday’s loss while catching another four passes for 17 yards. Barring any setback, we would expect him to be good to go for Week 12’s game against the Texans.

Source: Giana Han

item.title: Tyler Bass converted on 4-of-5 field goal attempts in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Tyler Bass BUF Kicker

Bass was the beneficiary of the Bills’ offense continuing to stall out once they got into the Dolphins’ territory. Bass made field goals of 43, 54, 40, and 28 yards on the day. However, the 29-year-old did miss a 54-yarder in the third quarter, which was his first missed field goal of the season. He’s now 24-of-25 on the season after missing all of last year with an injury.

item.title: Kyle Monangai rushed eight times for 18 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

Monangai played for the first time since suffering a turf toe injury in Week 4, getting 17 snaps on the day. He had five less carries and nine less snaps than D’Andre Swift as Salvon Ahmed also got involved with six carries for 33 yards. Monangai’s first snap was to run a route on third-and-long on the Bears’ first possession while he started in the backfield on the second drive. The 24-year-old had no receptions and just one red zone carry on the day, though his snap share and touch split with Swift was at pre-injury levels. Fantasy managers should anticipate less Ahmed usage in future weeks; Monangai should be in the RB4 ranks for Week 12 against the Lions.

item.title: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-7 targets for 12 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Greg Dulcich MIA Tight End

Dulcich saw the second-most targets on the team but ran a route on just 16 of the Dolphins’ 36 dropbacks. It’s nice to see Kyle McCord target him so often when he’s on the field, but Dulcich is not producing enough to be under consideration in fantasy leagues.

item.title: Joe Milton completed 11-of-21 attempts for 141 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers, adding five rushes for six yards.
item.description:
Joe Milton PHI Quarterback

Milton was in game manager mode as the Eagles maintained a lead throughout thanks to the team’s suffocating defense against Aaron Rodgers and the collapsing Steelers offense. Milton was not asked to do much, and he didn’t. He targeted DeVonta Smith — returning from a long injury absence — a team-high 12 times, missing him on a couple routine throws in the second half. Unless the Eagles face runaway negative game script, Milton won’t hold much fantasy value. He gets a good matchup next week against the Cowboys.

item.title: Chris Bell caught 1-of-4 targets for eight yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

Bell was questionable to return to the game after suffering a chest injury in the second quarter; however, he did return and ran 20 routes on 36 dropbacks, which was the third-most on the team. Bell still has a decent future given his pre-knee-injury upside, but it’s tough to roster him in redraft leagues right now.

item.title: Germie Bernard caught 6-of-10 targets for 40 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
item.description:
Germie Bernard PIT Wide Receiver

Bernard led the team in both pass routes and targets. He didn’t do much with his opportunity, which mostly included quick check-down passes from Aaron Rodgers. Roman Wilson returned from a finger injury and caught three balls for 43 yards while DK Metcalf was ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct in the third quarter. Max Hurleman, meanwhile, led the Steelers in receiving yards and caught the team’s lone touchdown while running just 15 routes. Bernard, who has 97 yards over his past four games, will be a deep league PPR option next week against the Broncos.

item.title: Malik Washington caught 3-of-6 targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Malik Washington MIA Wide Receiver

He also added two rushes for 11 yards. Washington made a tremendous one-handed catch on a fourth-down conversion late in the game, but there wasn’t much else happening for him on the day. His six targets were the third-most on the team, but he ran a route on 32 of the team’s 36 dropbacks, which was the most on the team. He’s a risky FLEX play against the Jets next week.

item.title: Dak Prescott completed 28-of-33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 51-30, Week 11 win over the Titans, adding four carries for nine yards and a fifth touchdown.
item.description:
Dak Prescott DAL Quarterback

Prescott totaled 10 touchdowns from Weeks 4-9. He’s now matched that total over his past two starts, including nine scores through the air. Today he found “the usual” of CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Javonte Williams for scoring strikes while tacking on role player Brevyn Spann-Ford. Prescott’s score on the ground was a lunge for the pylon where he was initially, confusingly labeled out of bounds. He was not, and the Cowboys’ unstoppable offensive effort marched on. Playing his best football just in time for Thanksgiving, Prescott will have the opportunity to stay hot vs. a short-handed Eagles D. Things then get dicier for fantasy managers, with the Cowboys visiting Seattle in Week 13 before an unseasonably late Week 14 bye.

item.title: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-6 targets for 62 yards in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

Coming off a month of quiet showings, this goes down as a rebound for LaPorta, even if it doesn’t do all that much for fantasy managers. LaPorta tied for a team-high in targets and trailed only Jameson Williams in yards. The only downside to his performance is that Brock Wright and Tyler Conklin combined for three catches and 60 yards. With a Thanksgiving shootout versus the Bears on tap, LaPorta will get one more game in the TE1 ranks for Week 12.

item.title: Caleb Douglas caught 2-of-10 targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

Douglas was the clear featured receiver in Miami’s offense this week, but it didn’t really amount to anything. On one possession, he was targeted on three straight passes in the end zone. He dropped one, was overthrown on one, and had the other broken up. He also had another drop on a pass inside Buffalo’s 20-yard line on the final drive of the game, but that wouldn’t have changed the outcome of the game at all. He should remain on the FLEX radar next week against the Jets.

item.title: Ollie Gordon II rushed 11 times for 69 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Ollie Gordon MIA Running Back

Gordon looked good in this one and consistently earned extra yards on his carries, but he simply didn’t get enough chances. Much of that is because Miami ran just 55 plays in this game and was trailing by two scores for almost the entire thing. Gordon should be in the RB2 conversation next weekend against the Jets.

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten exited the field in Week 11 against the Giants.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Tuten was dinged up on the first play of the game and was later seen riding the exercise bike on the sideline. He came into the game battling ankle and knee issues that limited him in practice this week. He may have aggravated the injuries. Chris Rodriguez would take over as the team’s lead back if Tuten misses time.

item.title: Jameson Williams caught all four of his targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs.
item.description:
Jameson Williams DET Wide Receiver

Williams busted his two-game slump with a 57-yard score in the third quarter. As he tends to do, Williams simply blew by the Bucs’ defense on a deep shot and saw nothing but grass in front of him. Despite the strong fantasy outing, Williams still finished fourth on the team in targets, behind all of the usual suspects. Williams has been one of the most frustrating fantasy options this year, but managers have to stick with him through the lulls to find spike weeks like today. He will be in the WR2 mix for a potential shootout with the Bears next week.

item.title: D’Andre Swift rushed 13 times for 51 yards and a fumble in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding two receptions for eight yards and a touchdown.
item.description:
D'Andre Swift CHI Running Back

Swift got the first three touches of the game for the Bears, operating as the lead back with Kyle Monangai back. His snaps took a dip, especially after a fourth quarter fumble. A shovel pass from Caleb Williams for a receiving score in the first half saved his fantasy production as Bears drives stalled frequently against the Saints. The good news is that Swift is still the lead back, though Monangai’s return will eat into his workload. Swift belongs in the fantasy RB2 ranks for a Week 12 Thanksgiving matchup against the Lions.

item.title: Roman Wilson caught 3-of-6 targets for 43 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
item.description:
Roman Wilson PIT Wide Receiver

Returning from a finger injury, Wilson ran a route on 41 of the team’s 59 drop backs and was second to Max Hurleman in receptions and receiving yards. Aaron Rodgers nearly connected with the speedy Wilson on a long ball in the second half. Wilson’s playing time may have been affected by DK Metcalf’s second half ejection after repeated fights with Philadelphia defenders. Wilson will have some deep league value in the run-first Steelers offense, including next week against the Broncos.

item.title: Dawson Knox caught 2-of-3 targets for 31 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Dawson Knox BUF Tight End

Despite Dalton Kincaid not being active on Sunday, Knox was not a huge part of the passing game. He did run a route on 29 of 52 dropbacks, which was fourth-most on the team, but he simply wasn’t targeted much. Kincaid is expected to return on Thursday against the Chiefs, which keeps Knox off the fantasy radar.

item.title: Keon Coleman caught 2-of-4 targets for 17 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Despite the return of Tyrell Shavers, who is a strong blocking receiver, Coleman ran a route on 45 of the team’s 52 dropbacks and played on 63 of 78 snaps. Both of those were a team-high. It didn’t result in fantasy success, but it seems like Coleman has evolved into the “dirty work” receiver in Buffalo who can move the chains with tough catches and pick up key blocks in the running game. He’s not a fantasy option next week against the Chiefs.

item.title: Simi Fehoko caught 1-of-5 targets for two yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
Simi Fehoko ARI Wide Receiver

He added three carries for seven yards. The 2021 fifth-round pick has suddenly become important at work, playing 47-of-49 snaps, but that does not mean he needs to be rostered in all but the deepest leagues given how poorly this offense is running.

item.title: Trey McBride caught 9-of-14 targets for 54 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
Trey McBride ARI Tight End

It sure does feel hard to find overall TE1 upside the past few weeks with Michael Wilson on the shelf. McBride was peppered with targets in the blowout loss but was mostly just an underneath option. His long gain went for just nine yards. McBride will remain a TE1 next week against the Commanders, but it’s fair to question the ceiling.

item.title: DJ Moore caught 8-of-10 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

There was a scary moment in the second quarter when Moore jumped to try and break up an interception and came down hard, hyperextending his knee. He went right into the locker room, and it seemed like he might be done for the day, but he came back out in time for the next drive. There’s a chance the Bills give him a lighter week of practice with the Chiefs coming up on Thursday, but Moore will need to be a big part of the game plan if Buffalo is going to win that game.

item.title: Caleb Williams completed 15-of-23 passes for 181 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception in the Bears’ 21-13, Week 11 win over the Saints.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

The Bears offense had its usual explosiveness, but struggled to finish drives. Williams’ mobility was on full display, using his legs to buy time and find receivers while adding 13 rushing yards before a pair of end-of-game kneels. He lofted up a fourth down end zone target to Kalif Raymond that was broken up in the first quarter and threw an interception in the second quarter. The drives that did end in touchdowns for the Bears in the first half came on a Williams shovel pass to D’Andre Swift and a toss to Colston Loveland in the flat he ran in for the score. Williams had completions of over 10 yards to five different receivers as he continued to push the ball downfield. His high-risk, high-reward style of play lends it self to splash plays to boost fantasy production. Williams will be in the low-end QB1 ranks for a Thanksgiving day matchup against the Lions.

item.title: Harrison Wallace caught 4-of-7 targets for 57 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
Harrison Wallace ARI Wide Receiver

It was the 2026 UDFA’s third game in the pros. He played 29-of-49 snaps. Wallace caught Arizona’s longest gain of the day, a 25-yarder. We guess we have to take the idea that Wallace could move towards FLEX value seriously as they move on to the Commanders in Week 12, but it is hard to imagine much fantasy value coming out of this team for the rest of the year outside of Trey McBride.

item.title: Chuba Hubbard rushed 27 times for 120 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Chuba Hubbard CAR Running Back

Hubbard didn’t see a target in this one, but he more than made up for his lack of targets with his efficiency on the ground. The 27-year-old back saw 15 of his 27 rush attempts go for four or more yards, and ripped off an 18-yard touchdown run in the second quarter for his first score of the day. He scored again in the third quarter on a one-yard touchdown run and added a two-point conversion, to the delight of his fantasy managers. Fellow running back Jonathon Brooks (groin) was close to suiting up in this one and could be back for Week 12 when the Panthers take on the Buccaneers on Monday Night Football. Despite Brooks’ impending return, Hubbard remains a must-start and will be in the RB1 conversation next week.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 23 times for 98 yards in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs, adding four catches for 20 yards.
item.description:
Jahmyr Gibbs DET Running Back

The Lions did a good job bottling Gibbs up for three quarters, but you can only keep him out of the end zone for so long. Gibbs punched in a one-yard score late in the fourth quarter to functionally seal the game. After a quick turnover-on-downs from the Bucs, he put the final nail in the coffin with another goal line touchdown. Gibbs entered the game tied for the league lead in touchdowns from scrimmage at 13. Now Christian McCaffrey needs to find the end zone twice to keep pace. Still putting up gaudy numbers every week, Gibbs is the unquestioned RB1 overall for his Week 12 game against the Bears.

item.title: Khalil Shakir caught 5-of-9 targets for 101 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Khalil Shakir BUF Wide Receiver

Shakir led the team in receiving yards and was second on the team in targets. He hauled in a 38-yard reception and a 32-yard reception, which fueled his day. One of those was on a long catch-and-run, and the other was on a broken play where Josh Allen was rolling out of the pocket and found Shakir. The 26-year-old receiver has a knack for getting open in space and will always be a big producer for Buffalo when they play defenses that like to play a lot of zone.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers completed 30-of-44 attempts for 227 yards and one touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding five rushes for 29 yards.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers PIT Quarterback

Rodgers, as he has been for most of the season, was wildly inefficient against the Eagles. He posted a -4.1 EPA, barely better than Joe Milton. Rodgers again was in check-down mode, only trying a couple deep shots and holding the ball time and again. Rodgers took five sacks and narrowly avoided a handful of others as the Steelers offensive line was overwhelmed for the second straight week. Coming into Week 11, only Daniel Jones and Baker Mayfield had lower drop backs EPAs than Rodgers. He’ll be a superflex option in Week 12 against the Broncos.

item.title: Derrick Henry rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers, adding four receptions for 17 additional yards.
item.description:
Derrick Henry BAL Running Back

Henry made the most of a plus matchup against a porous Panthers rush defense. The Big Dog’s 94 rushing yards were his most in any game since Week 5 against the Falcons, and he found the end zone on a 15-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter to put the Ravens up 33-32. Unfortunately, Henry landed hard on his head on the play and had to be taken to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion. While he didn’t return to the field, it was reported after the game that he cleared concussion protocol, meaning he should be in good shape to take on the Texans in Week 12. He will remain in the mix as a fringe RB1/RB2 for next week.

item.title: Jacoby Brissett completed 24-of-37 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Ravens’ 35-33, Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Jacoby Brissett BAL Quarterback

It was another up-and-down performance for Brissett, who missed a handful of easy throws, but also made the most of a Declan Doyle trick play call in the first quarter. On the play, Derrick Henry took the snap from the wildcat formation and immediately handed it off to Justice Hill, who pitched it back to Brissett on what looked like a flea-flicker off an end-around run. After taking the toss from Hill, Brissett immediately found Rashod Bateman downfield for a 52-yard touchdown pass. It would be the only touchdown Brissett would throw on the day, although he did lead the Ravens on two touchdown-scoring drives, one of which came on the heels of a 34-yard pass to Devontez Walker. Despite some decent moments, a late interception in the fourth quarter, as the Ravens were looking to get in range for a game-winning field goal, will be what fans remember most, as the Ravens have now lost six straight after getting off to a strong 4-1 start. Brissett will be on the QB2 radar next week when the Ravens visit the Texans in a battle between two teams who have underperformed expectations this season.

item.title: Tyler Allgeier rushed seven times for 23 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
Tyler Allgeier ARI Running Back

He out-snapped Bam Knight 26-23 in a committee that has managed to keep even a slim amount of fantasy value from coming to fruition. Allgeier has 259 rushing yards on the season if you exclude the week they played the Dallas Cowboys.

item.title: Ty Johnson caught 7-of-8 targets for 55 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Ty Johnson BUF Running Back

Despite his status as a running back, Johnson’s value to the Bills is as a receiver and pass blocker. He was a crucial option for Josh Allen when under pressure today, and Johnson consistently makes one or two big receptions in the screen game each week. His eight targets were third on the team this week, as were his 55 yards rushing. Still, it would be Ray Davis who would get a lot of rushing value if James Cook were ever to get hurt, which limits Johnson’s appeal as a stash option.

item.title: DeVonta Smith caught 5-of-12 targets for 41 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Returning from a two-month hamstring injury, Smith led the Eagles with a 57 percent target share. No other Eagles pass catcher saw more than five targets. Joe Milton missed a couple easy completions to Smith, one of which would have led to a chunk gain. It was a tough run-out for Smith, who looked fully healthy. Smith will be a solid option next week against a terrible Dallas secondary that was carved up by Cam Ward in Week 11.

item.title: James Cook rushed 22 times for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
James Cook BUF Running Back

With this effort, Cook has set an NFL record with nine consecutive games with 75+ rushing yards and a touchdown. Only two other players in NFL history had done it for eight games in a row. It’s the perfect encapsulation of Cook’s fantasy value on this Buffalo offense. The presence of Josh Allen will limit the number of touchdowns and ceiling games Cook puts together, but he remains one of the most consistent producers at the running back position in fantasy football. He remains an RB1, even in a tough matchup against the Chiefs.

item.title: Tyler Shough completed 25-of-42 attempts for 222 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Saints’ 21-13 Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding three rushes for 34 yards.
item.description:
Tyler Shough NO Quarterback

Shough and the Saints offense got off to another slow start. After a scoreless first quarter, Shough threw an interception in New Orleans territory in the second quarter. He was able to later connect with Alvin Kamara for a fourth-and-goal touchdown pass while a 30-yard scramble in the two minute drill led to a Saints field goal at the end of the half. The second half saw little offense from the Saints as they scored just one field goal the rest of the game. Shough failed to connect with Noah Fant on a crucial red zone fourth down and took a 13-yard sack in the two-minute drill at the end of the game. He averaged 5.3 yards per attempt in another inefficient showing. Shough belongs in the fantasy QB2 ranks for a Week 12 matchup against the Bengals.

item.title: Bryce Young completed 22-of-30 passes for 254 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Panthers’ 35-33, Week 11 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Bryce Young CAR Quarterback

Young and the Panthers had a much-needed bounce-back performance in Sunday’s win over the Ravens. After struggling to move the ball in Week 10’s win over the Saints, Young and the Panthers overcame an early safety on their opening drive to string together a nice five-play, 79-yard drive in the first quarter that included a 35-yard completion to Jalen Coker, which was followed by a 23-yard touchdown pass to tight end Mitchell Evans. In the second quarter, Young connected with Tetairoa McMillan for a seven-yard touchdown pass in the end zone to put the Panthers up 22-19 after Chuba Hubbard ran in a two-point conversion. Young’s lone interception came on another end zone target to McMillan in the third quarter, but the mistake didn’t prove too costly, as the Ravens went three-and-out on the ensuing drive. Young took back-to-back sacks to start a drive in the fourth quarter after the Panthers’ defense forced a turnover of their own, spoiling a chance to go up by two possessions, but the Panthers’ defense held up its end of the bargain late when it forced an interception of Jacoby Brissett to end any hopes of a comeback attempt. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, Young will be on the mid-to-high-end QB2 radar next week against the Buccaneers.

item.title: Bam Knight rushed seven times for 35 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs, adding a catch on his only target for 10 yards.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

Knight had three touches for three yards at halftime, but turned in a half-reasonable FLEX line once the Cardinals started running clock in the fourth quarter. He had 23 snaps to Tyler Allgeier’s 26. Even against the Commanders, this feels like a tough click in Week 12.

item.title: Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is inactive for Week 11 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers wasn’t spotted on the field during warmups, so he may not have been that close to playing today after all. He’s now eyeing a Week 12 return against the Browns. Michael Mayer will pick up a few extra targets versus Denver, putting him on the TE1/2 border. Also inactive for the Raiders are WR Dont’e Thornton Jr., WR Malik Benson, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, OG Bryce Cabeldue, and DT Tonka Hemingway.

item.title: The Jets declared Omar Cooper Jr., CB Jarvis Brownlee Jr., WR Isaiah Williams, LB Trevin Wallace, TE Jelani Woods and ED Nate Lynn inactive for Week 11 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

Removing Cooper and Williams leaves Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as the team’s top two wide receivers. Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could benefit as well. Geno Smith will play through his ankle injury today, after beginning the week in the questionable column. A run-heavy, quick-passing game plan could be incoming, given Smith’s ailment.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Chris Bell is questionable to return to Week 11 against the Bills with a chest injury.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

Bell and Bills safety Damar Hamlin collided on a Hamlin interception in the second quarter. It seemed like Bell and Hamlin slammed their helmets into one another, but Bell’s injury designation says chest. It’s been a season of tough injury luck for Bell, who has battled a knee injury all season after having offseason surgery.

Source: Omar Kelly

item.title: Charlie Kolar (concussion) is active for Week 11 against the Jets.
item.description:
Charlie Kolar LAC Tight End

Kolar, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden will form a three-player committee this afternoon. None of them warrant TE1 treatment, though they provide Justin Herbert with safety-blanket options and should help out in the run game.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Ladd McConkey (back) is active for Week 11 against the Jets.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey’s injuries have made him difficult to trust this season, but the Chargers have funneled targets his way when active. He should be viewed as a WR3 with volume-based upside, now evidently healthy enough to play. The Chargers declared LB Daiyan Henley, CB Tarheeb Still, WR Brenen Thompson, S Kendall Williamson, G Alex Harkey and WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith inactive for Week 11 against the Jets.

Source: Noah Furtado

item.title: Roschon Johnson suffered an ankle injury in the Bears’ Week 11 game against the Saints and is doubtful to return.
item.description:
Roschon Johnson CHI Running Back

Johnson was carted to the locker room in the first quarter against the Saints. He was announced to have an ankle injury and is doubtful to return. With Kyle Monangai back, the Bears had depth in the backfield again but lose a special teamer and third-string running back in Johnson against the Saints.

item.title: Lions declared CB D.J. Reed, CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr., DB Ketih Abney II, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, EDGE Tyrus Wheat, and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive for Week 11 against the Bucs.
item.description:
D.J. Reed DET Cornerback

Reed made seven starts this year before injuring his hip a few weeks ago. Rakestraw has been a depth option so far, but that would have been useful to have around with Reed out. The Lions’ defense will be as vulnerable as ever this week, though it’s anyone’s guess as to whether a hobbled Baker Mayfield will take advantage.

item.title: Dolphins declared S Dante Trader Jr., CB Jaylin Simpson, P Bradley Pinion, OL Christian Haynes, OL Caedan Wallace, TE Justin Joly, and WR Jared Wayne inactive for Week 11 against the Bills.
item.description:
Dante Trader MIA Safety

Trader Jr. is the Dolphins’ starting strong safety, but the rest of the inactives are depth pieces. Simpson does see the field as a backup cornerback, so the Dolphins will be down two members of the secondary in a game against Josh Allen, which is never great news.

Source: Marcel Louis-Jacques

item.title: Tyrell Shavers (knee) is active and will make his season debut in Week 11 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Tyrell Shavers BUF Wide Receiver

Shavers has been sidelined all season after tearing his ACL in a playoff win over Jacksonville last year. The 27-year-old had emerged as the team’s best blocking wide receiver last year and had seen his snap count increase as the season went on. He’s unlikely to be a fantasy factor, but it would not be surprising to see him play a decent amount of snaps once he is fully ramped up because of the value he provides in the running game. This means rookie Skyler Bell is back to being a game-day inactive.

Source: Matthew Bove

item.title: Dalton Kincaid is inactive for Week 11 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid was listed as questionable with (thumb/ankle) injuries, but he will not suit up. This makes sense as a cautionary move for the Bills, who already ruled out starting cornerback Christian Benford and starting linebacker Dorian Williams. The Bills are nearly a 17-point favorite against the Dolphins on Sunday and then will face the Chiefs on Thursday night. Except Dawson Knox to be more involved in this game in Week 11, but we wouldn’t be surprised if the Bills are running the ball a lot in the second half. The Bills’ full inactives are: WR Skyler Bell, TE Dalton Kincaid, OT Jude Bowry, DL T.J. Sanders, ILB Dorian Williams, OLB Mike Danna, and CB Christian Benford.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Roman Wilson (finger) is active for Week 11 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Roman Wilson PIT Wide Receiver

Wilson, who accounted for 16 percent of the Steelers’ targets and 39 percent of the team’s air yards before sustaining a finger injury in Week 5, will make his return to the lineup and likely make Germie Bernard all but unplayable in 12-team leagues. Wilson can be slotted in as a high-variance flex or second flex against the Eagles. The Steelers declared WR Kaden Wetjen, QBs Drew Allar Will Howard, Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, OLB Nick Herbig, and DL Gabe Rubio inactive.

item.title: Chiefs declared RB Kenneth Walker (groin) inactive for Kansas City’s Week 11 game against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

It’s Emmett Johnson szn once more. Also inactive for the Chiefs are QB Garrett Nussmeier (third quarterback), OL Jaylon Moore (ankle), OL Trey Smith (concussion), DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee), DT Peter Woods (neck) and CB Melvin Smith. Norman-Lott and Woods were both questionable and will not play. The others were ruled out on Friday.

item.title: Saints declared LB Pete Werner, CB Martin Emerson Jr., RB Audric Estime, OT Asim Richards, OT Taliese Fuaga, C Erik McCoy, and QB Zach Wilson inactive for Week 11 against the Bears.
item.description:
Audric Estime NO Running Back

Estime was seeing nearly half of the Saints’ backfield snaps up to last week. With Travis Etienne ramping back up from injury, the Saints choose to deactivate Estime, keeping Etienne as the primary back, Alvin Kamara as the pass-catching back, and rookie CJ Donaldson as the third-string in what has been a frustrating committee for fantasy purposes. Zach Wilson is the emergency third quarterback while Werner (hamstring), Emerson (concussion), Richards (knee), Fuaga (knee), and McCoy (biceps) are all out with injury, leaving the offensive line and defense short-handed against the Bears.

item.title: Titans declared RB Nicholas Singleton, LB Mohamoud Diabate, CB Jaylon Jones, DT Jackie Marshall and OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson inactive for Week 11 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Nicholas Singleton TEN Running Back

With Tyjae Spears on injured reserve, it’s a poor sign for fifth-round rookie Singleton that he is still getting healthy scratched in Week 11.

item.title: Darren Waller (knee) is active for the Panthers’ Week 11 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Darren Waller CAR Tight End

Waller was questionable with a knee injury entering the weekend, but will be good to go in what is somewhat of a revenge game against the team that drafted him in the sixth round back in 2015. The 34-year old tight end profiles as a boom-or-bust TE2 against a Ravens defense that has allowed the 10th-most PPR points per game (14.1) to opposing tight ends over its last five games. In addition to Waller, fellow tight end Tommy Tremble (knee) is also active, while TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, LB Bobby Okereke, C Sam Hecht, and DT TeRah Edwards will all be inactive for this one.

Source: Carolina Panthers

item.title: Cardinals declared QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas V, OL Kingsley Eguakun, OL Jon Gaines (ankle) and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Arizona’s Week 11 game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Josh Johnson ARI Quarterback

Just in case you were off the grid Saturday: Josh Johnson will start for the Cardinals against the Chiefs, becoming the fourth quarterback in four weeks for a team critics are calling “one of mankind’s most awful crimes.” OK, not really, but they are 15.5-point dogs. Johnson is probably one of the three worst superflex quarterbacks to have to start this week on a short slate.

item.title: Cowboys declared TE Jake Ferguson, OG Tyler Booker, S P.J. Locke, WR Jonathan Mingo, LB Jaishawn Barham and DT Jonathan Bullard inactive for Week 11 against the Titans.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Ferguson has barely played since Week 7. Although he is merely week to week with his ankle and knee issues, the formerly fantasy relevant seam stretcher seems unlikely to be a 12-team league factor down the stretch.

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is active for Week 11 against the Steelers.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Smith will finally make his return to game action after a two-month hamstring injury. Before the injury, he had accounted for 30 percent of the team’s targets and 47 percent of the team’s air yards. Smith’s 40 percent first-read target share was among the highest in the NFL over the season’s first month. He should be a decent WR3 here with Joe Milton under center. Eagles declared QB Cole Payton, CB Mac McWilliams, LB Smael Mondon Jr., LB Ajani Cornelius, and OL Jake Majors inactive against the Steelers.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Sione Vaki (ankle) is active for Week 11 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Sione Vaki DET Running Back

Vaki will continue to back up Jahmyr Gibbs, though that role hasn’t produced much fantasy value this year. He will only see a meaningful amount of touches if the Lions blow out the Bucs, which could happen. Vaki is buried in the RB5 ranks for now.

item.title: Bears declared QB Case Keenum, OL Jordan McFadden, CB Kyler Gordon, DL Jayden Loving, and LB Keyshaun Elliott inactive for Week 11 against the Saints.
item.description:
Kyler Gordon CHI Defensive Back

Gordon was already declared out with a shoulder injury heading into the weekend. Rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas (ankle) entered the day questionable, but will be active after missing Friday’s practice. Case Keenum will be the team’s emergency third quarterback.

item.title: Ravens declared CB Marlon Humphrey, FS Jaylinn Hawkins, RB Adam Randall, OG Emery Jones, DT Nnamdi Madubuike, and QB Kedon Slovis inactive for Week 11 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Marlon Humphrey BAL Cornerback

Humphrey, Madubuike, and Hawkins were all ruled out before the weekend. The Ravens will look to end a five-game skid in Jacoby Brissett’s second start with the team and face a Panthers defense that is near the bottom of the league at stopping the run, which could bode well for Derrick Henry and a ground game that has been stagnant in recent weeks.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Baker Mayfield (foot) is active for Week 11 against the Lions.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield is going to try to play through the plantar fascia injury he suffered in Week 9 before the Bucs’ bye. Expect the Bucs to lean on their ground game for as long as possible to protect Mayfield. Even in a good matchup, it’s hard to treat him as anything better than a mid-range QB2. EDGE Yaya Diaby is also active. Inactive for the Bucs are DT DeMonte Capehart, CB Ayden Garnes, OG Trevor Keegan, OG Billy Schrauth, QB Easton Stick, and S Antoine Winfield Jr.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports there is “not a lot of optimism” that Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) will play in Week 11 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers returned to practice earlier in the week and was listed as questionable on Friday. Schefter noted that Bowers is pushing to play, but we doubt the team will let him suit up after suffering another ankle injury. That’s on top of the quad issue, which seems to be minor compared to the ankle. Assuming Bowers is out, Michael Mayer should see an uptick in targets against a Denver defense that has bled fantasy points to tight ends this season. He would be a solid streaming option if Bowers is ruled out.

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Drake Maye (fractured fibula) is expected to miss at least six weeks.
item.description:
Drake Maye NE Quarterback

A six-week absence would technically allow Maye to return late in the regular season, but Rapoport then followed up by saying he has an “outside chance” at playing if the Pats make the playoffs. We suspect the Patriots would, at most, use the final weeks of the regular season to get Maye back on the practice field. Tommy DeVito is currently their starting quarterback and they’re sitting at 5-5, so a playoff berth doesn’t appear to be in the cards. Rapoport also mentioned Daniel Jones as an option in Maye’s absence. We doubt he saves New England’s season, but he would be an upgrade over DeVito.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Ravens offered the Colts a fourth-round pick for Daniel Jones and a conditional fifth-round pick.
item.description:
Daniel Jones

The fifth-round pick returned to the Colts if the Ravens made the playoffs. At worst, the Colts would have upgraded one of their Day Three picks. At best, they could have walked away with an extra fourth-round selection. They weren’t getting a king’s ransom for Jones, but it’s better than what they walked away with two weeks later when they cut him. The Colts’ mismanagement of the Jones situation will go down as a true blunder by a front office in disarray. Jones could still wind up in Baltimore as a free agent, assuming he clears waivers later this week.

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Davante Adams sounds like a “long shot” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Davante Adams

Adams isn’t expected to play in Week 12. The Rams get the Packers on Wednesday before Thanksgiving, and the tight turnaround makes a Week 12 return all but impossible. Head coach Sean McVay said Week 13 against Kansas City was a “possibility” earlier this week. That sounds unlikely now as well. Rapoport said Adams is eyeing a mid-December return. With Puka Nacua done for the year, the Rams are down to Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell as their top wide receivers for at least a few more weeks.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Micah Parsons is “on track” to play in Week 12 against the Rams.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

This isn’t a major surprise as head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Monday that he was hopeful Parsons would play in Week 12. It sounds like that timeline remains in the cards. Parsons has missed the first three months of the season while recovering from a torn ACL and meniscus injuries he suffered late last year. Getting Parsons back will be a huge boost for a Packers defense that hasn’t done much this year. Parsons had 12.5 sacks in 14 games with the Packers last year.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes Daniel Jones will “draw interest” from the Patriots and Ravens.
item.description:
Daniel Jones

Schefter didn’t directly cite his sources on this, so he may just be connecting dots. Still, the two teams make loads of sense for the downtrodden quarterback. The Patriots are expected to be without Drake Maye for at least the rest of the regular season. At 5-5, they’re still in the hunt for a Wild Card bid, though their odds of making the postseason will all but disappear if Tommy DeVito remains their starting quarterback. The Ravens are in a similar spot, though they’ve already addressed the quarterback position via Jacoby Brissett. Schefter notes that the most likely outcome is that Jones waits for a more attractive spot to open up. He is expected to clear waivers later this week, at which point he will become an unrestricted free agent.

Source: ESPN

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Colts are shutting down Alec Pierce (heel) for the remainder of the 2026 season.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

Pierce signed a four-year, $114 million contract in the offseason. He almost immediately underwent surgery and was expected to miss three months, though it took a bit longer than that. There was also a mix-up about whether or not he underwent a second PRP injection, which at-the-time GM Chris Ballard denied. He was sidelined for a bit longer than that but did play in Week 1. Pierce then re-injured his heel in Week 2, functionally ending his season. The team has now chosen to shut him down to avoid any chance of further complications. It sounds like he will be good to go for 2027. Pierce’s season ends with five catches for 72 scoreless yards. He will return to a rebuilding Colts roster that is unlikely to support his WR3 fantasy case next year.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Baker Mayfield (foot) will play in Week 11 against the Lions.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield looked unlikely to play after missing Wednesday’s practice. He inexplicably returned for Thursday’s session before being listed as questionable the next day. He’s dealing with a plantar fascia injury that hobbled him in the team’s Week 9 loss to the Bears. A Week 10 bye was just enough time off to get him back on the field without any time missed. Even in a great matchup with the Lions, it’s hard to trust Mayfield as anything other than a mid-range QB2.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) will play in Week 11 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans’ agent posted a video on his Instagram that can only be described as the corniest thing you will see today. In it, he vaguely announced that Evans was back after missing a few weeks with Achilles tendinitis. Evans will likely be managing this injury for the rest of the season, so we wouldn’t be surprised if he returns on a bit of a pitch count. Still, Evans was operating as the team’s unquestioned WR1 before suffering the injury. He will be on the WR2/3 border for his first game back.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (MCL surgery) will be sidelined 4-5 months.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

This confirms Nacua will not only miss the remainder of the regular season, but would be unavailable for any potential Super Bowl run for the pre-season favorites. Schefter did add that Nacua’s knee “checked out clean aside from the MCL.” That’s good news heading into Nacua’s potential free agency, though he is nevertheless at a low ebb in his up-and-down Rams tenure. The ups have been any time Nacua takes the field. The downs have been how often he has been sidelined, as well as his off-the-field issues. Going on 26, Nacua would make a lot of sense as a franchise tag candidate, or perhaps a tag-and-trade for the Rams.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Panthers ruled out Jonathon Brooks (groin) for Week 11 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

Brooks will miss his seventh consecutive game in Week 11, leaving Chuba Hubbard to a true workhorse role for another week. The matchup is less than ideal against the Ravens but fantasy managers can continue riding the bump in volume to a high end RB2 profile for the veteran back.

item.title: Kyren Williams (toe) was limited Saturday but is expected to play in Week 12 against the Packers.
item.description:
Kyren Williams

Williams is reportedly dealing with “soreness” in his toe and was limited in practice Saturday as a result. ESPN’s Sarah Barshop added that Williams is expected to play on Wednesday against the Packers. Expect him to continue working in a strict timeshare with Blake Corum coming out of the team’s Week 11 bye.

Source: Sarah Barshop

item.title: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful for Week 11 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Andrei Iosivas CIN Wide Receiver

Iosivas was practicing in full throughout the week, making his designation somewhat puzzling as he attempts to return from injured reserve. The team will have another week to activate the young wide receiver before he will be forced to remain on injured reserve for the remainder of the season.

item.title: Eagles placed WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Wicks has already missed the previous three games with an ankle injury and now finds himself sent to injured reserve, meaning he will miss at least seven games total with poorly timed injuries. He saw a “foot” designation added to his status during a week of limited showings, which is presumably the issue that lands him on injured reserve. DeVonta Smith, who returns from an extended absence this week, Makai Lemon, and Darius Cooper are likely to hold down the starting wide receiver positions in Wicks’ absence.

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play in Week 11 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks surprisingly went from a full session Thursday and a no-show Friday, prompting uncertainty regarding his expected availability for Monday Night Football against the Bengals. He quickly put those worries to rest with a full practice Saturday and was removed from the injury report. Expect Burks to continue operating in a featured role on the perimeter in the absence of Terry McLaurin.

item.title: Rachaad White (heel) is questionable for Week 11 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Rachaad White WAS Running Back

White’s week of practice was troubling, first appearing on the injury report on Friday with a limited designation due to a heel ailment before being downgraded to a “DNP” Saturday. Even so, head coach Dan Quinn indicated the veteran back is “on track” for Monday Night Football. Assuming he is active, White is likely to slot back into the primary change of pace role behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt, the latter of whom appears set to be activated from injured reserve in time for Monday.

item.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is questionable for Week 11 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

Croskey-Merritt managed a week of full practices as he attempts to return from injured reserve, and while the team has not yet activated him, he appears to be trending in the right direction for his first game action since Week 5. Rachaad White, also listed as questionable, would likely shift back to a primary change of pace role, should Croskey-Merritt return.

item.title: Steelers did not activate Michael Pittman (foot) ahead of Week 11.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman will remain on injured reserve for at least another week. The team gets back fellow wide receiver Roman Wilson, who should join DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard as the starters from 11-personnel. Fantasy managers are likely only able to confidently start Metcalf against the Eagles.

item.title: Steelers activated WR Roman Wilson (hand) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Roman Wilson PIT Wide Receiver

Wilson ended up staying on injured reserve for the minimum four games as he dealt with a hand injury, returning to a roster approaching full health, although fellow wide receiver Michael Pittman was not activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 11.Fantasy managers are likely only able to confidently start Metcalf against the Eagles on Sunday.

item.title: Cardinals ruled out Carson Beck (back) for Week 11 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

That paves the way for 36-year-old journeyman quarterback Josh Johnson to draw the start under center for the Cardinals after being added to the team less than two weeks ago. Dynasty managers will be forced to wait longer for the first extended look at the third-round rookie as the Cardinals continue forward with insurmountable injuries up and down their roster in what has quickly become a lost season. Downgrade the primary skill position players in a difficult matchup against the Chiefs in Week 11.

item.title: Titans placed RB Tyjae Spears (knee) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he tends to a knee injury that has plagued him in recent weeks. Spears previously missed two games in Week 7 and Week 8 before returning to a modest workload in Week 9 after the team’s bye. Tony Pollard should continue operating in a true workhorse role and gets one of the top matchups in the league against the Cowboys in Week 11. Fantasy managers can continue to treat Pollard as a volume-driven RB1 after a slow start to the season.

item.title: Commanders HC Dan Quinn told reporters RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is “trending the right way” ahead of the matchup with the Bengals in Week 11.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

Quinn said Croskey-Merritt had a great week and is trending the right way for Monday’s game against the Bengals. It’s great news for fantasy managers and the Commanders as backup running back Rachaad White (heel) missed practice Saturday. Croskey-Merritt deserves FLEX consideration assuming he’s active against the Bengals this week.

Source: Ben Ständig

item.title: Rachaad White (heel) missed practice on Saturday.
item.description:
Rachaad White WAS Running Back

White was added to the injury report and was a limited participant in practice on Friday. His missed practice Saturday is another bad sign for the 27-year-old running back’s availability. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) trending towards being available, White doesn’t seem to have much fantasy value at the moment. CB Amik Robertson, who was seen limping in the locker room on Friday, also missed practice Saturday.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Titans WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) is likely to return against the Cowboys in Week 11.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

Tate hasn’t played since Week 7 due to a shoulder injury. Still officially questionable, Zenitz reports Tate is likely to play in Week 11. While he’s been out for over a month, Tate got in a full practice on Friday. He’ll be a high-end WR3 in a plus matchup against the brutal Cowboys defense.

Source: Matt Zenitz

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield (foot) is dealing with a plantar fascia injury.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

While Mayfield remains on track to play against the Lions on Sunday, he’s dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury, according to Pelissero. If the 31-year-old gunslinger suits up in Week 11, he’ll wear a special orthotic and new cleats to help stabilize his foot. Mayfield looked doubtful to play earlier in the week and even missed practice Wednesday before getting in a pair of limited sessions. Jalon Daniels would start if Mayfield isn’t able to play this week.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler described Rams WR Puka Nacua’s future with the team as “very uncertain.”
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nothing earth-shattering here from Fowler. Appearing on ESPN’s SportsCenter Saturday morning, the NFL Insider noted that Nacua is dealing with a significant MCL injury and a three-game suspension from the NFL. With Nacua unlikely to return this season, Fowler says this isn’t the kind of momentum the 25-year-old receiver wanted heading into free agency, where he’ll be the best player available. The Rams can extend him, franchise tag him or let him hit the open market this offseason. As Fowler says, it’s something the Rams have to sort out.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Mike Evans (Achilles) “is trending in the right direction” for Week 11 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Rapoport does note, however, that Evans is “a little sore” after returning to practice on Thursday. The 49ers will make a decision on Evans’ Week 11 status on Saturday. If active, Evans will carry some re-injury risk, but reports have consistently indicated that the 49ers learned a lot from Christian McCaffrey’s bilateral Achilles tendinitis in 2024. It seems safe to assume that if Evans is active, his Achilles tendon is in good shape. Evans may not immediately return to his pre-injury form against the Vikings’ elite defense, but he should be in fantasy football lineups.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Puka Nacua’s (knee/toe) recovery timeline “does not match up” with a potential return for Super Bowl LXI.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua is currently on injured reserve, recovering from MCL and PCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury. He will also serve a three-game suspension on injured reserve, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye. The superstar wide receiver underwent surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday, and Rapoport believes we have “almost certainly” seen the last of Nacua in the 2026 season. He is set to enter free agency this offseason, and it is unclear whether the Rams will extend him, franchise tag him or allow him to walk.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes the Patriots and Ravens are “potential landing spots” for Daniel Jones.
item.description:
Daniel Jones

Jones seemingly has decent odds of passing through waivers unclaimed, but he would be free to sign with any team after that. Rapoport adds that Jones is “still working his way back” from last year’s Achilles tendon rupture in his right, plant leg. Jones had a $10 million injury guarantee in his contract that is said to have been a factor in his release. Were he to sign with the Patriots, he could compete for the starting role with Tommy DeVito. Jacoby Brissett would probably be able to fend him off initially, were he to land in New England.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Team reporter Darren Urban believes Josh Johnson will “probably” start in Week 11 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Josh Johnson ARI Quarterback

Rookie Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms again, so recently signed journeyman Johnson will likely get the start this week. Urban notes that Johnson “played significant snaps for LaFleur in two games for the Jets in 2021, " completing 55-for-81 passes for 621 yards, five touchdowns and two interceptions. With six teams on bye, Johnson, 40, is in the low-end QB2 conversation.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is not on the Broncos’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Talanoa Hufanga DEN Safety

Hufanga has not played since Week 5. He nearly returned in Week 9, pre-bye, but was unable to do so. His return could be helpful for a Broncos’ defense that struggles to cover tight ends. Broncos S Brandon Jones (hamstring) is questionable to play, and CB Riley Moss (concussion) is good to go.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Charlie Kolar (concussion) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 11 game against the Jets.
item.description:
Charlie Kolar LAC Tight End

Kolar had not practiced either of the first two days of the week before this sudden Friday revival where he got in a limited session. We’d be surprised if he ultimately played coming off a short week, but no Chargers tight end is ultimately compelling with or without Kolar in the lineup.

item.title: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 11 game against the Jets.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey was limited in all three sessions this week and was a shadow docket rule out in Week 9 while being a straight inactive in Week 10. Actually practicing ahead of this game is a sign things are better, but he’ll be no more than a WR3 in this dilapidated passing attack between the re-injury risk and the lack of upside. Yes, even against the Jets.

item.title: Isaiah Likely (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Isaiah Likely NYG Tight End

Likely sat out on Friday after practicing in full, injury-free, on Wednesday and Thursday. With six teams on bye and very few reliable tight end options in fantasy, Likely remains in the TE1 tier. Monitoring his status throughout the weekend will be worthwhile. Hopefully, we continue to get positive reports on his groin injury. Likely notably dealt with a groin injury back in Week 5.

Source: Mia O’Brien

item.title: Matt Gay (hip) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 11 game against the Broncos.
item.description:
Matt Gay LV Kicker

Kansei Matsuzawa is on the Raiders’ practice squad and would presumably be elevated if the team rules out Gay. Neither player seems especially likely to be a good fantasy bet this week against the Broncos with a rookie quarterback under center.

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ladd McConkey (back) is expected to play in Week 11 against the Jets.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey experienced back spasms in pre-game warmups two weeks ago. The Chargers didn’t announce that until the game had started and he did not play a snap. The team had the courtesy to rule him out ahead of kickoff last week. He got in three limited sessions this week before being listed as questionable. McConkey has been the Chargers’ most effective wideout when healthy, but that has been an exceedingly rare occurrence this year. We suspect he’s still not at full strength. With the risk of a re-injury looming, fantasy managers should treat him as a WR3, even if his ceiling his much higher.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Bud Dupree has requested his release from the Chargers.
item.description:
Bud Dupree LAC Outside Linebacker

Fowler also reveals that Dupree asked to be released in the offseason, but the Chargers have been unwilling to grant it. Dupree is playing infrequently and has just two quarterback pressures and one tackle. Releasing him would reduce their depth, but he is not a critical defender for this 1-8 squad. Stay tuned.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Chris Rodriguez is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

With Bhayshul Tuten not on the report either, Rodriguez looks likely to reprise his role as a clear backup against the Giants. He will not be worth gambling on in the FLEX spot without dramatic Tuten news ahead of Sunday.

item.title: Rachaad White (heel) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Friday.
item.description:
Rachaad White WAS Running Back

Mid-week additions to the injury report are generally a bad sign for a player’s availability. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is also practicing in full, potentially pushing White into the droppable tier once tomorrow’s official injury report is released. Stay tuned.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers got in three limited sessions and will continue to play through this ailment. The Jaguars haven’t been tested enough to get him out of the WR4 ranks for the last few weeks, but if the Giants come to play on offense on Sunday, perhaps that will change.

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Tuten got in a limited session on Wednesday, a DNP on Thursday while working with trainers, and appeared to do much the same on Friday before getting an official “limited” designation. Clearly gutting his way through the injury at this point, Tuten will remain a high-end RB2 against the Giants.

Source: Ryan O’Halloran

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

This could just be a rest day. Burks played through the injury last week, logging just one limited session, and he was clearly limited by the injury in-game. He still has a chance to play in this week’s Monday Night Football game against the Bengals, but he would be a terribly volatile FLEX if so.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Zack Baun (back) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
item.description:
Zack Baun PHI Linebacker

Baun didn’t practice at any point this week and could be in rough shape for a short-week Thanksgiving game against the Cowboys as well.

item.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) is questionable for Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

Illness was an added designation today. While it normally probably wouldn’t matter, since Shipley is already on injured reserve, the Eagles can afford to take it slow with him if they’d like to. If active, Shipley won’t be a FLEX play with Saquon Barkley healthy.

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

He got in full sessions each of the last two days to clear the report. With Joe Milton under center, Smith is more of a WR3 than a WR2 at this point, but with six teams on bye fantasy managers can’t be choosy.

item.title: Carson Beck (back) is questionable to play in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback
