Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters earlier today that Beck is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs, so this may just be a formality. If active, Beck would be a low-end QB2 this week despite six NFL teams being on bye. Josh Johnson is expected to start in his stead.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Wicks got in three limited sessions, but notably had the “foot” ailment attached to him after it only being listed as an “ankle” the last two days. It’s possible this is nothing major and the Eagles are just taking it easy with him, but a new injury should be on the radar. Wicks has little fantasy utility either way at this stage.

item.title: Jets ruled out Isaiah Williams (ribs) for Week 11 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Isaiah Williams NYJ Wide Receiver

This is unfortunate. Williams had a chance to play a larger role with Omar Cooper (ankle) sidelined. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell benefit from these players’ absences, though they will be catching passes thrown by a hobbled Geno Smith (ankle).

Source: New York Jets

item.title: Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) will not play in Tampa’s Week 11 game against the Lions.
item.description:
Antoine Winfield TB Safety

Winfield, who popped up with this injury on Wednesday, did not practice at any point this week. Yaya Diaby (knee) is questionable but probably on the optimistic side of it after getting in a full session on Friday. Tristan Wirfs practiced in full all week and is not on the final injury report with his toe ailment.

item.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been ruled out for Week 11 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

Cooper and Isaiah Williams (ribs) will both miss this week’s game, leaving Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to lead the wide receiver corps. Both players’ target share projections should increase a tad. Cooper did not practice at all this week. He has dealt with multiple ankle injuries in his rookie season.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: Baker Mayfield (foot) is questionable for Tampa Bay’s Week 11 game against the Lions.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield got in two limited sessions after missing Wednesday with the injury. Todd Bowles spoke to reporters earlier today and said that he was “trending in the right direction” to start this week. He seems to be on the optimistic side of questionable, Jalon Daniels would grab the start if Mayfield is unable to go.

item.title: Geno Smith (ankle) is not on the Jets’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Geno Smith NYJ Quarterback

The Jets’ starting quarterback was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation on Friday. Smith has turned in a couple of decent games this season, but he’s currently on a two-game skid in which he has failed to beat 165 passing yards and/or throw a touchdown. He is stuck in the QB2 tier despite six teams being on bye this week.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: D.J. Reed (hip) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 11 game against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
D.J. Reed DET Cornerback

He got in limited sessions all three practice days this week and seems to be trending in a good direction after missing Week 9 and Week 10 with this hip injury. He’s probably best-regarded as a game-time decision.

item.title: Cade Mays (ankle) will not play in Detroit’s Week 11 game against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Cade Mays DET Center

It seems rather unlikely that Mays will be able to get up off the mat for Week 12’s Thanksgiving game as well on a short week. Juice Scruggs will continue to start for the Lions for the time being.

item.title: Chiefs ruled out RG Trey Smith (concussion) for Week 11 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Trey Smith KC Guard

Smith and RT Jaylon Moore (ankle) will both miss this week’s game against the Cardinals, but the Chiefs should be able to manage the situation. There is a decent overall talent gap between the two teams. Kansas City faces the Bills next week. Hopefully, the right side of the offensive line is ready for that one.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 11 game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears hit the questionable line with this knee injury in Week 10, Week 7 and Week 6 before this latest one. Given how similar the pathing looks to last week’s — as he also got in a full session ahead on Friday here — we think he’s more likely to play than not. He’s probably only a desperation FLEX play in a good matchup against the Cowboys busted run defense.

item.title: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 11 game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

The big news here is that he got in a full session on Friday after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. The long layoff is still a little bit concerning, but a full session likely inches him over to the optimistic side of questionable in what looks to be a shootout. Tate will have high-end WR3 appeal if he’s able to go.

item.title: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Vega Ioane BAL Guard

He got in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday. Hopefully his return will help calm down the interior of the Baltimore offensive line. The Ravens will need all the pass protection help they can get if they keep playing as they did on Monday night.

item.title: Chris Bell (knee) is not on Miami’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

He’ll play against the Bills. It’s not exactly a smash play after he missed last week’s game with some soreness in his surgically-repaired knee, but it’s certainly plausible that Bell will be in the fantasy discussion in Week 12 if he proves healthy and able this week.

item.title: Dee Alford cleared concussion protocol and is not on Buffalo’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Dee Alford BUF Cornerback

He’ll be tasked with slot work against the Dolphins with Christian Benford (groin) out. It’s good news for Buffalo D/ST streamers that they’ll at least have one of Buffalo’s better corners back for this one.

item.title: Caleb Douglas (shoulder) is not on Miami’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

He got in a full session to evade the questionable line on Friday. With Buffalo’s banged up secondary and the run attack sliding to a halt without Malik Willis under center, it’s plausible that Douglas can cook up some real numbers this week. He is RotoPat’s 23rd ranked receiver this week as of Friday afternoon.

item.title: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) will not play in Dallas’ Week 11 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Ferguson has now missed two weeks with this injury and has not practiced at all in the interim, leaving his status for a short turnaround Week 12 highly questionable. It is wheels up in the TE2 ranks for Brevyn Spann-Ford.

item.title: Chiefs ruled out Kenneth Walker (groin) for Week 11 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

The Chiefs face the lowly Cardinals this week, but they face the Bills next week. Allowing Walker to fully heal in time for that important matchup makes sense. Stud rookie Emmett Johnson remains a fantasy football RB1 after an explosive showing against the Falcons last week. Walker will vault back into the RB1 tier upon returning.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is questionable for Week 11 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

We do not yet know Bowers’ Friday participation level. He was seen at practice, and Kubiak told reporters that Bowers got “a lot of work in.” Some reports indicate that Bowers spent time away from his teammates, working with trainers, though, so he could end up being a limited participant. The Broncos struggle to cover tight ends effectively. If active, Bowers is an elite TE1, albeit with some re-injury risk.

Source: Sam Warren

item.title: Roman Wilson (hand) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Eagles.
item.description:
Roman Wilson PIT Wide Receiver

He got in three full sessions this week and seems likely to be activated off injured reserve — most IR activations this season have received a questionable tag regardless of how often they’ve practiced. With the depth back in their receiving corps on Sunday (assuming Michael Pittman is also activated), we’d probably fade the non DK Metcalf pass catchers against Philadelphia and see how things sort out. It’s certainly not impossible that Wilson produces real fantasy value down the stretch despite the competition.

item.title: Nick Herbig (ribs/hip) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Eagles.
item.description:
Nick Herbig PIT Linebacker

He did not practice at all this week, though it’s possible he’s just going to be able to play through the pain on Sunday and the Steelers are taking it easy on him. Patrick Queen (hand) is also questionable, but got in a full session on Friday and we’re optimistic about his chances of returning.

item.title: Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Eagles.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman got in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday after a limited practice on Wednesday. It would not be surprising at all if he were activated for this game ahead of Sunday, though we wouldn’t quite call it a certainty. If he does come back, he may serve more as a governor for Germie Bernard than as someone you’re excited to start in fantasy right away.

item.title: Dre Greenlaw (neck) is questionable to play in Week 11 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Dre Greenlaw SF Linebacker

We do not yet know Greenlaw’s Friday participation level. He was limited on Thursday, and the 49ers tacked on a “Not injury-related - resting player” tag to his listing. The fact that he is questionable indicates the neck injury is a factor. Perimeter CB Renardo Green (back) will play. Slot CB Upton Stout (shoulder) is questionable.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Kyler Murray (hamstring) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 11 game against the 49ers.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

It’s his third straight week on the shelf. Carson Wentz will again handle backup duties behind Kirk Cousins.

item.title: T.J. Hockenson is not on Minnesota’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

He can be fired up as a low-end TE1 with Jordan Addison (finger) out for the foreseeable future. Hockenson got in limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday before a full session on Friday tipped him past the questionable line.

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes signing Daniel Jones could be an option for the Patriots.
item.description:
Daniel Jones

Drake Maye has been diagnosed with a fractured fibula and is expected to be sidelined “deep” into the regular season. Tommy DeVito replaces him as the team’s starter. He is backed up by seventh-round rookie Behren Morton, who has reportedly “made a positive impression.” Jones has played poorly this year, prompting a surprise release earlier today. Despite the poor play, Jones still might be able to outplay DeVito and the late-Day 3 rookie. Assuming Jones passes through waivers, he could make sense as an affordable bridge option for the Patriots.

Source: ESPN

item.title: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
CJ Donaldson NO Running Back

He’ll return to his pass-blocking role for the Saints, assuming they want him active, in Week 11. No fantasy value here for the moment.

item.title: Jordyn Tyson (chest) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

He got in a full session on Friday and was cleared off the report for Week 11’s game against the Bears. He’ll be an upside WR3 after last week’s 13-target breakout against the Panthers.

item.title: Jeffery Simmons (knee) is not on Chicago’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Jeffery Simmons CHI Defensive Tackle

Simmons practiced in full on Friday after being limited with a knee listing the last two days. It wouldn’t be surprising if he continued to be limited in practice after this game given the quick turnaround to Chicago’s Week 12 Thanksgiving game against the Lions.

item.title: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) will not play in Chicago’s Week 11 game against the Saints.
item.description:
Kyler Gordon CHI Defensive Back

He was ruled out after three straight missed practices following the Week 10 bye. It does not look especially likely he’ll be able to turn it around next week and play in Chicago’s Thanksgiving game against the Lions.

item.title: Kyle Monangai (toe) is not on Chicago’s final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

He’ll return to FLEX plausibility as the Bears take on the Saints in a game where a crockpotting run-heavy attack is certainly in the range of possibilities. Monangai has not played since Week 4, but has fully recovered from a turf toe injury and practiced in full all three days this week. He shouldn’t have any limitations.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans (Achilles) was questionable for San Francisco’s Week 11 game against the Vikings.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

We don’t have a practice status yet, but the 49ers said they’d make a decision on Evans’ status on Saturday. If active, he’ll be a reasonable WR3 bet due to the risk of in-game injury management risk and the tax the Vikings defense enacts on opposing passing games.

Source: Matt Barrows

item.title: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Taliese Fuaga (knee) will not play in New Orleans’ Week 11 game against the Bears.
item.description:
Taliese Fuaga NO Tackle

Asim Richards (knee) was also ruled out, leaving the Saints with 24-year-old UDFA Mason Murphy as a potential Week 11 starter at tackle.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that A.J. Brown (hamstring) is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

According to Reiss, Brown would normally be a candidate to land on injured reserve, but the Patriots are already close to the limit of how many players they can designate for return from injured reserve. The Patriots are on bye this week. Were Brown to be placed on injured reserve, he would be eligible to return for the Patriots’ Week 16 game against the Jets after missing four games. Although he will remain on the active roster, Reiss’ comments suggest Week 16 could be Brown’s expected return date. For fantasy leagues with an injured reserve spot, Brown is worth holding onto. For leagues that lack an injured reserve spot, it might make sense to drop him for a fill-in starter at the running back spot, or a player of equivalent value.

Source: ESPN

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Drake Maye fractured his fibula and it is expected to sideline him “deep into the regular season if he is able to return this year at all.”
item.description:
Drake Maye NE Quarterback

Maye is being given the Jaxson Dart Memorial Puncher’s Chance of returning, but it doesn’t look likely that he’ll return this year and, if you were holding out hope for whatever reason, he can be dropped in most re-draft leagues at this time. Maye won’t have to undergo surgery and there was no additional ligament damage. The Patriots may choose to not put Maye on injured reserve because they are already near the limit of how many players they can designate to return.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Bills coach Joe Brady said Christian Benford (groin) will not play in Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Christian Benford BUF Cornerback

Neither will Dorian Williams (calf) who also missed practice most of the week. Neither player is regarded as having a long-term injury, per Brady, so they should have a chance to get up for Week 12’s Thanksgiving game against the Chiefs.

Source: Lance Lysowski

item.title: Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 11 game against the Panthers.
item.description:
Nnamdi Madubuike BAL Defensive Lineman

Madubuike did not practice all week after injuring the hamstring on Monday night. A prolonged absence wouldn’t be surprising, but the Ravens have been tight-lipped about it so far.

item.title: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Isaiah Likely (undisclosed) is dealing with a “minor” injury.
item.description:
Isaiah Likely NYG Tight End

Likely was noticeably absent from Friday’s practice, but Harbaugh said he expects his tight end to be okay. We assume that means he will be fine for Sunday’s game against the Jaguars, but we will need to wait to see where things stand when the team releases its final injury report on Friday. We should have a better sense of what he is dealing with soon, but in the event he can’t go, Theo Johnson would be the next man up to replace Likely.

Source: Dan Duggan

item.title: Bills coach Joe Brady said Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is doubtful for Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid has not practiced yet this week and we’re guessing from this designation he won’t be heading to the field on Friday either. This has, sadly, become pretty standard for Kincaid as he simply has to be managed week-to-week on the injury report. Dawson Knox should join the TE2 ranks for Week 11 assuming Kincaid is out, though it’s plausible Kincaid’s fantasy managers can do better on the wire.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Richardson will start in Week 12 against the Giants.
item.description:
Anthony Richardson IND Quarterback

The surprising release of Daniel Jones immediately thrusts Richardson back into the QB1 role, a role he hasn’t held since 2024. The former No. 4 overall pick now has a chance to make the most of what is a lost season for the Colts, who are fresh off a 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night. Richardson has played sparingly this season, completing 2-of-4 passes for eight yards while rushing three times for six yards. Playing in an offense that’s devoid of weapons at receiver, the Colts would benefit from leaning into Richardson’s ability as an athlete by utilizing him in the ground game. Richardson’s rushing upside could eventually put him on the radar as a decent QB2, but we will conservatively project him as a low-end QB2/QB3 in his first start in over two years.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Colts waived QB Daniel Jones.
item.description:
Daniel Jones

Well, the Colts apparently evaluated everything, as they said they would last night. Wow. Jones makes it 11 games into a two-year, $88 million contract. He will be subject to waivers since the trade deadline has passed. It’s possible — though we’d be hard-pressed to say likely given the $2 million owed this season, $10 million next year and $38 million in non-guaranteed 2027 cash — that someone takes a chance on the deal. If not, he’ll be free to sign anywhere for the rest of the season. Minnesota would probably take a gamble on him again after they scooped him up in this same exact manner a few years ago, but that’s just speculation on our part. It’s stunning in the sense that it happened in-season, but this was obviously the way things had been trending as Indianapolis’ offense simply hasn’t been able to operate with Jones. Anthony Richardson will take over as the starting quarterback for the time being.

Source: Colts

item.title: Tommy Tremble (knee) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Tommy Tremble CAR Tight End

Tremble got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday after missing Wednesday. He’s probably best regarded as a true question mark, though nobody’s fantasy lineup should be riding on him being inactive or not. Tremble would be a reasonable TE2 play if he were able to go.

item.title: Darren Waller (knee) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Darren Waller CAR Tight End

He got in two limited practices on Thursday and Friday. You’re probably not planning to play either he or fellow questionable tight end Tommy Tremble as anything more than a TE2 either way. If both players were somehow ruled out, Mitchell Evans would take their place in the pecking order.

item.title: Jets rule out Omar Cooper (ankle) for Week 11 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

Cooper and Isaiah Williams (ribs) will both miss this week’s game, leaving Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to lead the wide receiver corps. Both players’ target share projections should increase a tad. Cooper did not practice at all this week. He has dealt with multiple ankle injuries in his rookie season.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

Brooks practiced in full all three days this week and we’ve seen players pacing to be activated off injured reserve be given this soft questionable listing several times this year. Expect Brooks to play as Chuba Hubbard’s main backup. He’ll likely be brought along slowly in his first game back.

item.title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck (back) is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

According to Cardinals beat writer Darren Urban, LaFleur “won’t close [the] door on Beck just yet,” but the team is preparing as if Josh Johnson will draw the start on Sunday against the Chiefs. This was already shaping up to be a disastrous matchup for the Cardinals, and an offense that is down its top three receivers, and this isn’t doing anything to help the situation. If they weren’t already doing it, fantasy managers everywhere should be scrambling to stream the Chiefs defense in what is shaping up to be a very favorable home matchup.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Rams head coach Sean McVay said “there is a possibility” Davante Adams (hamstring) plays in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Davante Adams

The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported last week that the Rams were “hopeful” this would be the timeline for Adams’ return. McVay somewhat confirmed that optimism while speaking to the media on Friday, but noted that the star receiver isn’t “ready quite yet.” This follows McVay announcing that Puka Nacua (knee) will miss the next few months after MCL surgery, so it’s safe to assume the Rams will be thin at receiver in Week 12 when they take on the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.

Source: Michael J. Duarte

item.title: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (foot) is “trending” in the right direction to start in Week 11 against the Lions.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield reportedly looked good in Friday’s practice and logged back-to-back practices to close out the week. We should have an update on his official game status soon, but all signs are pointing to him starting this week against a Lions team that has allowed the fifth-most passing yards this season. We will check back in with an official update when the team provides it.

Source: Scott Smith

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) was seen practicing on the side field on Friday.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

This will presumably result in a DNP for Tuten this week, but we’ll see what the team announces when it releases its final injury report. According to Jaguars beat writer Ryan O’Halloran, Tuten was on the field with his helmet to stretch with teammates during warmups but then went to the side field. If he is listed as a DNP, it would be the second straight day Tuten failed to get on the practice field, but he could still receive a questionable designation entering the weekend. We will check back in with a final status update once the team announces it in a few hours.

Source: Ryan O’Halloran

item.title: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua will undergo surgery on his MCL and will be out “a couple months.”
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Shortly after it was reported that Nacua “will undergo” surgery, we learned that the star receiver actually had surgery on Tuesday. We don’t know exactly how long Nacua will miss, but it’s safe to assume his only path back for the 2026 season would be if the Rams make a run in the postseason. Even then, his recovery timeline could be too long for a late-January/early-February return. The 25-year-old receiver was in the midst of another stellar season for the Rams, catching 70 passes for 715 yards and four touchdowns in the seven games he appeared in. Nacua is in the final year of his four-year rookie contract and is on track to receive a lucrative payday this offseason, presumably from the Rams. An offseason marred by off-the-field issues and a stint at a rehab facility likely delayed the decision to extend him before training camp, but Nacua continues to play at an elite level on the field. If all goes well, it sounds like he should be healed well ahead of training camp next offseason.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Baker Mayfield (foot) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield will close out the week with back-to-back practices, which should give him a decent chance at playing in Week 11’s game against the Lions. Things looked doubtful for Mayfield earlier in the week, especially after the Bucs signed Cooper Rush to the practice squad on Monday. We should get official word on Mayfield’s status shortly, but it’s safe to say he is trending in the right direction at this point.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he will “evaluate everything” at QB after Daniels Jones’ poor outing in Week 11’s loss to the Texans.
item.description:
Daniel Jones IND Quarterback

Steichen didn’t commit to Jones as the Colts’ Week 12 starter for next week’s game against the Giants. Anthony Richardson replaced Jones late in Thursday night’s loss to the Texans, but the Colts have been reluctant to bench Jones, despite a disastrous season in which he has thrown for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns, and 13 interceptions. It feels like a switch to Richardson is inevitable at some point. With some extra time to prep him for next week’s game, now could be the time to make the move back to the former No. 4 overall pick.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Geno Smith (ankle) is trending toward playing in Week 11 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Geno Smith NYJ Quarterback

We should have the final word on Smith’s status shortly, but Glenn said his QB1 will log another practice on Friday, which should be enough for him to play on Sunday against the Chargers. Smith has struggled in recent weeks, throwing for 313 scoreless yards, but could have a chance to bounce back against a woeful Chargers defense that has allowed the 10th-most passing yards and the fifth-most net yards per attempt this season.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Isaiah Williams (ribs) will not play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Isaiah Williams NYJ Wide Receiver

Williams could have been in line for a decent workload given that Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/hip) has been ruled out, but the 25-year-old receiver will join Cooper on the sidelines for this one. Veteran Tim Patrick, who ran 22-plus routes in Weeks 5 and 6 when the Jets were shorthanded at the position, could be next in line for playing time, but he should probably be avoided even on a week with six teams on bye.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

This was to be expected. Cooper was bounced from Week 10’s game against the Bills after one snap, after he had his ankle rolled up on, and has not gotten on the practice field this week. The 22-year-old receiver has had a challenging start to his career and is now slated to miss his fifth game of the season. Fellow receiver Isaiah Williams (ribs) has also been ruled out, paving the way for Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to have busy days against the one-win Chargers. It doesn’t sound like Cooper is at risk of being placed on injured reserve, so we’ll see if things fare any differently for him entering Week 12.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: Xavier Hutchinson caught 2-of-3 targets for 13 yards in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
item.description:
Xavier Hutchinson HOU Wide Receiver

Hutchinson’s three targets were a product of a game environment dominated by the Houston defense, with no player seeing more than the five targets accounted for by alpha wide receiver Nico Collins. Fantasy managers that were riding the recent production from Hutchinson were surely left disappointed in the down performance, with his next opportunity to return a usable fantasy outing coming in a Week 14 meeting with the Ravens. It remains to be seen whether Marvin Harrison Jr. will make it back in time for that contest, something that could influence the upside of Hutchinson in a zone-heavy matchup.

item.title: Tank Dell caught 3-of-4 targets for 27 yards in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
item.description:
Tank Dell HOU Wide Receiver

Dell was blanked in the first half before seeing three consecutive plays drawn up for him in the third quarter, catching all of them for his complete yardage total on the evening. The team continues to take a conservative approach with the young speedster after he missed more than a year with one of the more gruesome injuries you will see, holding his fantasy value in check in the process. Dell can likely be stashed for the potential he sees his route rate increase later in the season but is likely best left on fantasy benches for the time being.

item.title: Kayshon Boutte caught both targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
item.description:
Kayshon Boutte HOU Wide Receiver

Boutte’s two targets were a product of minimal pass volume in a game the Texans were able to control with their defense. He made the most of the modest volume by coming down with a touchdown in the second quarter on a dime delivered by quarterback C.J. Stroud to the middle of the end zone from 24 yards out, catching the ball with the defender draped around his midsection. Boutte remains a shaky fantasy bet as nothing more than the third option through the air, with the team expecting to get back newcomer Marvin Harrison Jr. from a hamstring injury in short order. That could come as early as Week 12 considering the Texans now get a long week of preparation ahead of a meeting with the Ravens.

item.title: Nico Collins caught 3-of-5 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

Collins caught two passes, one of which went for his 42-yard touchdown, on the team’s second possession before being subject to modest pass volume due to increasingly positive game script. His touchdown grab will most certainly make an appearance on highlight reels for some time, mostly due to quarterback C.J. Stroud’s performance on the play. Stroud shrugged off a strong-side pass rusher to quickly reset his feet and deliver a strike downfield to Collins, turning a potential sack into a touchdown with the flick of his wrist. He appeared to effortlessly heave the ball 50 yards through the air without being able to step into the throw, placing the football where only Collins could catch it over the defender. Collins remains one of the league’s top talents at wide receiver but is subject to performances like this when the Texans are able to control games with their defense, which is exactly what transpired here. Up next for Collins and the Texans are the Ravens in Week 12, where the veteran receiver will remains an upside WR2 due to modest volume expectations.

item.title: David Montgomery rushed 26 times for 107 yards in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts, adding 17 yards on three receptions.
item.description:
David Montgomery HOU Running Back

Montgomery shook off a relatively slow start to reach 100 yards on the ground for the first time as a member of the Texans, doing so with Woody marks inactive due to a concussion. Veteran journeyman Emari Demercado handled just seven touches as the primary change of pace option. Montgomery churned out consistently positive yardage but managed just one explosive run, a 15-yard scamper to ice the game late in the fourth quarter. No longer a featured back at this point in his career, the 100-yard showing could go down as his top fantasy performance of the season with Marks expected back from injury when the Texans face the Ravens in Week 12. Treat Montgomery as a potential Flex option in that matchup.

item.title: C.J. Stroud completed 21-of-27 passes for 194 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Texans’ 26-3, Week 11 win over the Colts, adding 27 yards on six carries.
item.description:
C.J. Stroud HOU Quarterback

Stroud’s lone mistake came on the team’s first possession of the game when a poorly thrown ball over the middle of the field intended for Nico Collins was picked off. He would go to work from there, completing nine of his next 10 passes while throwing two touchdowns before the half. A 17-3 lead at the break saw a slight uptick with a safety on the defense’s first time on the field in the second half, with Stroud tacking on his third touchdown throw on the following possession. The team would go into coast mode from there, eventually chasing Daniel Jones from the game with just over seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, with Stroud finishing with three or more touchdown passes for the fourth time in his last five appearances. Stroud and the Texans get the floundering Ravens in Week 12, where he will remain a back end QB1 in fantasy circles.

item.title: Tyler Warren caught 1-of-5 targets for 22 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans.
item.description:
Tyler Warren IND Tight End

The poor showing comes on the heels of a two-catch, one-yard performance in Week 10, leaving fantasy managers scratching their heads following the departures of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline. Warren briefly departed in the second quarter after being shaken up on his lone reception but returned to do absolutely nothing else for the remainder of the game. The Colts gained only 165 yards of total offense with Daniel Jones under center through almost 53 minutes of play, something that has become a routine occurrence of late. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the starting quarterback ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Giants before considering entering Warren into lineups. Even so, there appears to be no good option currently on the roster.

item.title: Ashton Dulin caught 2-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans.
item.description:
Ashton Dulin IND Wide Receiver

Both of Dulin’s receptions came on the opening possession of the game, with a 25-yard catch down the sideline sparking the drive that led to the team’s only points. The Colts remain a veritable disaster at present, leaving nobody on the weekly fantasy radar - Dulin most certainly included.

item.title: Anthony Gould caught 2-of-3 targets for 48 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans.
item.description:
Anthony Gould IND Wide Receiver

Gould played sparingly despite the recent wide receiver departures, with his team-leading 48 yards more a statement on the current state of the offense than anything else. Nobody on this sinking team deserves fantasy consideration, a sentiment that extends to its depth pieces.

item.title: Jonathan Taylor rushed 11 times for 21 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans, adding six yards on four receptions.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

Taylor went as the rest of the offense went in this one, with the team gaining just 165 yards of total offense through almost 53 minutes of play with Daniel Jones under center before the veteran signal caller was replaced by Anthony Richardson. The only points mustered for the duration of the contest came on the opening possession of the game, sparked by a 25-yard completion to Ashton Dulin down the sideline. Taylor again rotated with Seth McGowan in a 1A-1B situation until the latter was forced from the game with a hamstring injury sustained on a kick return to end the first half. The team has no reason to run Taylor into the ground in a lost season, significantly capping his fantasy value in the process. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the starting quarterback for the Colts entering a Week 12 meeting with the Giants before inserting Taylor into lineups.

item.title: Daniel Jones completed 12-of-27 passes for 144 yards and an interception in the Colts’ 26-3, Week 11 loss to the Texans, adding three yards on one carry.
item.description:
Daniel Jones IND Quarterback

Jones led the Colts to only 165 yards of total offense through almost 53 minutes of play against the Texans, also taking a sack in the end zone for a safety, before being replaced by Anthony Richardson with just over seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. This is the second game in the previous four weeks in which Richardson has come on in relief of an underperforming Jones in the fourth quarter. When you add that to the continuous questions fielded by head coach Shane Steichen surrounding the quarterback position moving forward, pressure appears to be mounting toward a potential change under center in a lost season. For what it’s worth, Richardson came on and immediately threw a pass that should have been intercepted during a quick three-and-out possession, which were the only three plays he ran as the Texans controlled the ball to run out the clock. Fantasy managers should not have held on for this long, but it is safe to say that Jones can be returned to the waiver wire from whence he came.

item.title: Seth McGowan (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 11 against the Texans.
item.description:
Seth McGowan IND Running Back

McGowan pulled up lame following a kick return at the end of the first half and was deemed questionable to return when the two teams came out after the break. Jonathan Taylor appears to be in line to operate as a true workhorse for the remainder of the game after McGowan had carved out a meaningful role the previous two weeks. McGowan managed seven yards on three carries and caught his lone target for one yard prior to departing.

item.title: Anthony Gould (toe) is active for Week 11 against the Texans.
item.description:
Anthony Gould IND Wide Receiver

Gould will play through his toe injury this evening, but he is on a boom-bust WR5. The Colts are playing without both of their starting offensive tackles, and Gould is not a replacement-level starter.

Source: Indianapolis Colts

item.title: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Colts want their next general manager to have a say in Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones’ futures with the team.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

The Colts have faced scrutiny for their decision to keep Taylor and Jones on the roster, rather than trading one or both away for draft picks. Palmer said this is about empowering their next general manager. The team has reportedly compiled a preliminary list of candidates, potentially putting the team in position to make a hire quickly after the season. Stay tuned.

Source: James Palmer

item.title: T.J. Hockenson (wrist) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

Hockenson has a chance to return from his wrist injury for the Vikings’ Week 11 game against the 49ers. It would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If active, Hockenson will likely qualify as a low-end TE1 with six NFL teams on bye this week.

Source: Minnesota Vikings

item.title: Caleb Douglas (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

Douglas is still limited despite coming off the Dolphins’ Week 10 bye, but he has a chance to play this week against the Bills. He will be catching passes thrown by Kyle McCord, but with six teams on bye, Douglas is at least in the FLEX conversation this week.

Source: Miami Dolphins

item.title: Chris Bell (knee) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

Bell reportedly hyperextended his knee last week, hence his day-to-day labeling this week. Bell had been limited from time to time already this year by soreness in his surgically repaired knee. The fact that this is unrelated is actually good news. He has a chance to play in Week 11 against the Bills.

Source: Joe Schad

item.title: Colts declared CB Sauce Gardner, QB Riley Leonard, TE Will Mallory, LT Bernhard Raimann, DT Jerry Tillery, RT Jalen Travis and CB Charvarius Ward inactive for Week 11 against the Texans.
item.description:
Sauce Gardner IND Cornerback

Gardner and Ward are the Colts’ starting perimeter cornerbacks, and Raimann and Travis are the Colts’ starting offensive tackles. Losing all four for this game will be consequential. The Texans’ wide receivers and pass rushers should play efficiently in this week’s Thursday Night Football game.

Source: Indianapolis Colts

item.title: Texans declared Marvin Harrison, EDGE Danielle Hunter, RB Woody Marks, TE Brevin Jordan, C Jake Andrews, OG Wyatt Teller and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 11 against the Colts.
item.description:
Marvin Harrison HOU Wide Receiver

Harrison (hamstring) and Marks (concussion) are both out this week, condensing the Texans’ skill position corps for fantasy football purposes. Both players can be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues, though neither player is a must-stash option. David Montgomery should handle a sizable workload with Marks out.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Ladd McConkey (back) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver is tentatively on track to play in Week 11 against the Jets, but ideally he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow. The Chargers have been willing to run the passing offense through McConkey when he is active. He is a WR2, albeit with some re-injury risk, if he suits up.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans has a chance to play in Week 11 against the Vikings. If active, Evans should be in fantasy football lineups. Re-injury risk is possible, but the 49ers have handled this issue smartly. We should have a decent indication as to whether he will make his return by tomorrow evening. Stay tuned.

Source: Josh Dubow

item.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Wicks is stuck in the questionable column, but he still has a chance to play. With QB3 Joe Milton at the helm, Wicks would only be a WR4/5 against the Steelers in Week 11. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Will Shipley (foot) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

Shipley could need another week to fully recover from his injured reserve-worthy foot injury. Shipley partially tore his plantar fascia just over a month ago. Once he is active, he will likely serve as the Eagles’ No. 2 running back.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Zack Baun (back) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Zack Baun PHI Linebacker

Baun is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 11 game against the Steelers. If he is unable to play, the Steelers’ rushing attack should have a slightly easier time moving the ball. Stay tuned.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Excellent news. The Eagles’ No. 1 wide receiver is on track to face the Steelers in Week 11. Although he will be trying to catch passes from erratic QB Joe Milton, Smith’s target volume should keep him in the WR2 tier. It is possible that the team keeps him on a snap count, but he will be featured when he is on the field.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Isaiah Williams (ribs) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Isaiah Williams NYJ Wide Receiver

Williams’ injury is unfortunate because Omar Cooper (ankle) is seemingly unlikely to play. If Williams were able to go this weekend, he would enter the boom-bust FLEX tier with six NFL teams on bye. Hopefully, he practices tomorrow.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

The Jets’ rookie wide receiver is on the wrong side of questionable. He appears to be likely to miss this week’s game against the Chargers. Ankle issues have bothered him for some time. Perhaps taking a week off would benefit him in the long run. He remains a worthwhile hold at this time.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: Geno Smith (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Geno Smith NYJ Quarterback

Smith is tentatively on track to play in the Jets’ Week 11 game against the Chargers, though his mobility could be somewhat impacted if this is indeed the case. Smith would warrant QB2 treatment if active. He is backed up by Cade Klubnik.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: Carson Beck (back) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

Beck’s back issues continue. The rookie quarterback has dealt with this for weeks now. He should be viewed as questionable to play in the Cardinals’ Week 11 game against the Chiefs. Journeyman QB Josh Johnson is his backup.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers resumed practicing in a limited capacity today, and although his quad ailment was not reported early in the week, it is not new. The Raiders listed him with both ankle and quad injuries yesterday as well, which likely explains why Bowers had such a hard time returning to the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. He is tentatively on track to face the Broncos this weekend.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Packers released RB Pierre Strong.
item.description:
Pierre Strong

We take this move as a good sign for Josh Jacobs’ (finger) health. Strong could end up being signed to the Packers’ practice squad. He played a rotational role for Green Bay this season, leading the team with 17 opportunities in Week 6.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Antoine Winfield (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Antoine Winfield TB Safety

The Buccaneers’ stud safety is trending toward a Week 11 absence. His team faces the Lions this week. Fortunately, Buccaneers LT Tristan Wirfs (toe) is practicing in full and should be good to go.

Source: Rick Stroud

item.title: Ray Davis (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Ray Davis BUF Running Back

Davis is still worth stashing on benches in 12-team leagues. He is James Cook’s primary backup. Passing down specialist Ty Johnson (knee) is practicing in full this week and should be good to go.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Christian Benford (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Christian Benford BUF Cornerback

Benford and Bills LB Dorian Williams (calf) remained sidelined today. Bills slot CB Dee Alford (concussion) resumed practicing in a limited capacity, but he is still firmly in the questionable camp. The Bills can probably sneak past the Dolphins if a few of their defenders are absent, but having them on the field is obviously ideal.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

This is a little concerning. Backup plans should be made at this time. Kincaid played through the ankle injury in Week 10 against the Jets, but evidently picked up a thumb injury along the way. Dawson Knox would only be a TE2 if Kincaid sits, but the Dolphins’ defense is hardly imposing.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Dalton Risner (knees) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Dalton Risner CIN Guard

The Bengals’ stud right guard is dealing with injuries to both knees. Hopefully, the extra day of rest leading up to this week’s Monday Night Football game allows him to get healthy enough to play. The offense is better with him active.

Source: Jay Morrison

item.title: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Andrei Iosivas CIN Wide Receiver

Iosivas is seemingly on track to play in Week 11’s Monday Night Football game against the Commanders, but he does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins (knee), Chase Brown and Mike Gesicki are playing very well in the receiving game.

Source: Jay Morrison

item.title: Tee Higgins (knee) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Tee Higgins CIN Wide Receiver

Higgins injured his knee in Week 10 against the Steelers, but apparently it is only a minor injury. The Bengals’ No. 2 wide receiver is having an excellent season, and that top-tier performance should continue against a beatable Commanders’ pass defense. Higgins is a borderline WR1/2 with six teams on bye.

Source: Jay Morrison

item.title: Joe Burrow (illness) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

Burrow should be able to face the Commanders in this week’s Monday Night Football game without issue. Fortunately, his No. 2 wide receiver, Tee Higgins (knee), is also practicing in full this week. Burrow is an elite QB1.

Source: Jay Morrison

item.title: Jordyn Tyson (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

It’s back-to-back limited sessions for Tyson, leaving him likely on the optimistic side of questionable heading into Friday’s practice sessions. Tyson will be an upside WR3 against the Bears in Week 11 based on the volume he was commanding last week so long as he avoids any unexpected setbacks on Friday.

item.title: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Vega Ioane BAL Guard

The Ravens’ talented rookie guard continues to practice and play through two difficult injuries. Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) remains sidelined through two Week 11 practices. Ioane should be able to face the Panthers this weekend. Madubuike could be sidelined.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers has been rolling through this ankle issue the last few weeks and the fact that he remains limited shouldn’t be considered worrisome. He’ll be a fringe WR3 with six teams on bye in Week 11.

item.title: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

Rodriguez has now gotten in back-to-back limited sessions. The veteran backup would slide into an enviable spot if Bhayshul Tuten were unable to go after Tuten’s Thursday DNP, but we’d be surprised if it wound up that way after Tuten played through these injuries the last few weeks. If Tuten is active, Rodriguez is just a rough FLEX play, even with six teams on bye.

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

He was spotted on the sideline with trainers, and he has played through this injury each of the last two weeks. That makes us optimistic that a rug pull won’t be forthcoming on Friday. Still, the Friday practice participation line has yet to be written and it is a negative trend after Wednesday’s limited session.

item.title: Carnell Tate (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

Tate has now gotten in back-to-back limited sessions, though the fact that he’s coming off three weeks lost (two games, bye) leaves us a little unsure if we should say he’s “trending” towards playing. A full session would be nice to see and we’d be surprised if he cleared the questionable line on Friday without one.

item.title: Tyjae Spears (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. The Cowboys/Titans game has been looking like it’ll be a shootout if the Titans can keep up their end of the bargain, and six teams are on bye. Even with that, we still can’t muster much FLEX excitement for Spears as Tony Pollard’s backup.

item.title: Nick Herbig (ribs/hip) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Nick Herbig PIT Linebacker

Herbig is on the wrong side of questionable for the Steelers’ Week 11 game against the Eagles. Hopefully, he can get healthy before long. Patrick Queen (hand) remains limited, but he is on track to play this weekend.

Source: Mike DeFabo

item.title: Kenneth Walker (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

It’s looking like it will be another RB1 ranking for Emmett Johnson against the Cardinals this week. Walker has not been on the field for either of the first two practices of the week and if there’s a coach on the team or a #SourcedMen claiming he has a real chance to play, we haven’t seen it yet.

item.title: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman is tentatively on track to return in time for the Steelers’ Week 11 game against the Eagles. In his three games played from Weeks 1-3, Pittman caught seven passes for 89 yards. He will only be a WR4/5 when he returns to the field, though the Steelers do not currently have a starting wide receiver who is reliably producing. It is possible for him to carve out a role in the coming weeks.

Source: Mike DeFabo

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks missed Week 9 and played through this injury in Week 10, and it seems like the extra rest after Thursday Night Football has done him some good. If he can overtake Chig Okonkwo as the No. 2 target in Washington’s passing game down the stretch, perhaps there’s some reasonable fantasy value to be had.

item.title: Chig Okonkwo (back) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo left last Thursday night’s game against the Giants briefly with an injury scare, but had returned by the end of the game. This listing tells us he’s in no danger of missing Monday Night Football and, assuming Ben Sinnott isn’t suddenly usurping him as the starter after his nice game, Okonkwo can be played as a fringe TE1.

item.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

Pretty much all the smoke here is that he’ll be activated and ready to go for Monday Night Football and the injury report does not disagree with that assertion. We’re expecting to see him as questionable on the final injury report because that is just generally how teams label players returning from IR, but ‘Bill’ is looking like a reasonable FLEX play against the Bengals.

item.title: Jordan Schultz reports the Saints plan to release S Justin Reid at his request.
item.description:
Justin Reid

Reid’s having his worst season in the league per PFF’s charting data, having compiled a 49.1 PFF defensive grade and his second-worst coverage grade as a pro at 47.8. That said, Reid has plenty of versatility and wants to seek work with a contender. It sounds like he’ll likely find a new home in the near future.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Puka Nacua will serve a three-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy while on injured reserve.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Schefter notes that the timing of Nacua’s suspension “could potentially save him a substantial amount of money.” Suspended players are not paid, and Nacua is in the final year of his rookie contract. Serving the suspension now “will cost him a lot less than serving it on his next contract, which is expected to be far more lucrative.” Schefter does not say whether he thinks the Rams will be the team that pays him, but a big payday is apparently still expected. Players are required to miss four games on injured reserve. Nacua has already missed one game. The Rams are on bye this week. He will spend the remainder of his injured reserve stint while also serving his suspension, and he will be eligible to return for Week 15 against the Cowboys. Nacua will be allowed to rehab his injuries at the Rams’ facility for the suspension’s final two weeks.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Kyler Gordon CHI Defensive Back

Gordon, the Bears’ starting slot cornerback, is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s game against the Saints. Bears DT Jeffery Simmons was limited by a knee injury, but DC Dennis Allen said he does not expect the injury to impact Simmons’ availability.

Source: Brad Biggs

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes that the Titans or Chargers would host “an auction” for the 2027 NFL Draft’s No. 1 overall pick if either team gets it.
item.description:
Cam Ward TEN Quarterback

The Titans are currently in position to receive the No. 1 overall pick, and the Chargers are right behind them. Schefter spent much of the segment discussing the Titans, who Schefter says have “enough conviction” in Cam Ward that they would pass on the opportunity to draft Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker. He cites the Dolphins, Jets, Cardinals and Browns as potential suitors. Poor play from Ward could still change minds in the Titans’ front office, but for now, it seems as though his job is secure.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Tommy Tremble (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Tommy Tremble CAR Tight End

Tremble, who had 48 yards last week against the Saints, is probably the preferred TE2 play between himself and Darren Waller if both players make it to Sunday’s game against the Ravens healthy. Each of them logged a limited session on Thursday after missing Wednesday.

item.title: Darren Waller (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Darren Waller CAR Tight End

He didn’t practice Wednesday, so this is a good sign for his availability. With Tommy Tremble also practicing though, we may remain in the Panthers TE Stasis where both players are taking too much volume off the table for you to want to start either of them in fantasy leagues.

item.title: Brock Bowers (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

This is great to see. We expect Bowers to be listed as a limited participant, but his return to practice with an extra day to spare gives him a real chance to suit up in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that routinely surrenders catches and yardage to the tight end position. Bowers is an elite TE1 if active.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that the Colts have a “package of plays in the playbook” for Anthony Richardson, but it is unclear whether they will “ever” use them.
item.description:
Anthony Richardson IND Quarterback

Holder stops short of making any declarative statements, but today’s article implies that some in the Colts’ organization may be wondering why their 24-year-old quarterback hasn’t at least been used as a situational player. Holder compares Daniel Jones’ poor play to positive remarks made by Colts defenders regarding Richardson’s explosive dual-threat abilities. Holder does note that the Colts have at least considered using Richardson’s “electric running ability” to give them “a spark,” but for whatever reason, that hasn’t happened yet. Richardson could be worth stashing in superflex leagues, though there is no guarantee that he will take the field on game day.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker said he considered leaving the Cowboys after being stripped of play-calling duties.
item.description:
Christian Parker DAL Defensive Coordinator

Parker was demoted after the Cowboys got rocked by the 49ers in Week 10. Defensive assistant Mike Pettine will call plays on defense for now. When asked about his future in Dallas, Parker could only say he will cross that bridge when he gets there. It sounds like he and the Cowboys will part ways after the season. Parker was a defensive backs coach in Denver and Philadelphia for five seasons before landing the Dallas defensive coordinator gig.

Source: Calvin Watkins

item.title: Broncos signed CB Riley Moss to a four-year, $67 million contract extension.
item.description:
Riley Moss DEN Cornerback

The former third-round pick played almost exclusively on special teams as a rookie. He took over a starting role in his second season and never looked back. Moss has eight pass breakups and one interception this year. He led the league in PBUs in 2025. Moss was set to hit free agency next offseason. Instead, the Broncos got out ahead of him hitting the open market and kept him in town on a relatively affordable deal. Moss is just outside the 20 highest-paid corners on a per-year basis.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Baker Mayfield (foot) returned to practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield did not practice Wednesday after injuring his foot ahead of the Bucs’ Week 10 bye. It initially looked like he would miss his Week 11 game against the Lions. Now he might be on the right side of questionable. Mayfield was spotted going through ball security drills and hopping over pads early in the practice. He certainly looked like a quarterback who was preparing to play in a few days. Mayfield hasn’t been all that productive this year, but he would still be an upgrade over Jalon Daniels. This is a situation to monitor heading into the weekend. After his limited practice today, Mayfield told reporters that he feels “ready” to play on Sunday, though the team has not made an official ruling. Stay tuned.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: The Baltimore Ravens sent Marlon Humphrey home and he will be inactive for Week 11.
item.description:
Marlon Humphrey BAL Cornerback

Humphrey was asked what the city of Baltimore was good at making on his personal podcast, The Marlon Humphrey Show. He jokingly responded, “They’re the best at making criminals.” Humphrey has since apologized for the disparaging remark, but the team is dismissing him for the week after a wave of backlash. He could potentially return in Week 12 against Houston.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: 49ers GM John Lynch said “there’s a chance” Mike Evans (Achilles) practices on Thursday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

We’ll know more in a few hours, but even a chance at practicing is a small step in the right direction for Evans. The veteran wideout hasn’t played since Week 6 because of his Achilles tendinitis. We still expect this to be a ramp-up week of practice for him before returning in Week 12, but there’s at least an outside shot of him suiting up on Sunday.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Christian Kirk underwent a successful meniscus surgery.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

Rapoport didn’t give any details on Kirk’s timeline to return. We suspect he is done for the season. Kirk missed most of the season with a hamstring injury. He returned for one game, didn’t record any stats, and then injured his knee. Kirk signed a one-year deal with the 49ers in the offseason. He will be stuck taking another prove-it deal if he’s healthy when free agency starts in the offseason.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Commanders signed WR Malik Heath to the practice squad.
item.description:
Malik Heath WAS Wide Receiver

Heath worked out for the Commanders Wednesday and signed to the practice squad. He caught 31 passes for 308 yards and three touchdowns over the past three seasons with the Packers and spent some time with the Falcons as well last season. The Commanders add Heath as receiving depth for the practice squad.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Daiyan Henley (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Daiyan Henley LAC Linebacker

Henley infamously was sent back to the Chargers after a reported trade with Denver fell through due to a failed physical. He returned to play in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens, but now misses the first practice of the week with a knee issue. Given he has been playing through soreness, Henley’s absence may just be load management after a Monday game. Henley still has a chance to play in Week 11 with practices later in the week.

item.title: Ladd McConkey (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey has been dealing with the back injury for two weeks now, sitting out the Chargers’ last two games. He continues to deal with a various set of injuries and is a wild card when it comes to playing on game days. A limited designation at least gives fantasy managers hope that he will play in Week 11 against the Jets, though McConkey has fallen to unreliable WR3 status at this point of the season.

item.title: Charlie Kolar (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Charlie Kolar LAC Tight End

Kolar seemingly came out of the Chargers’ first win of the season with a concussion, though he was on the field up until making the game-sealing catch on the last drive. He will need to clear concussion protocol in order to be eligible for Week 11 against the Jets. Also not practicing was WR Brenen Thompson (hamstring). Neither player has fantasy impact, though Kolar’s blocking is important for a Chargers team with a banged-up offensive line.

item.title: Dre Greenlaw (neck) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Dre Greenlaw SF Linebacker

Greenlaw popped up on the injury report with a neck issue and did not practice on Wednesday. He dealt with a knee issue last week but played through it in Week 10. Practice reports later in the week will clarify the severity of Greenlaw’s neck issue as his Week 11 status is in jeopardy for now.

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle exited the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers with a concussion. He had time to work through the protocol with a Week 10 bye and is now back to practicing at the start of Week 11. Given his full participant listing, Waddle is trending to play this week against the Raiders. He has had a disappointing fantasy season and should be in the WR3 ranks for Week 11.

item.title: Zack Baun (back) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Zack Baun PHI Linebacker

Baun watched practice from the sidelines in street clothes today. He was briefly the subject of trade rumors at the deadline, but nothing materialized. Baun will play if healthy this week, but we don’t expect him to be rushed back in the midst of a lost season for the team. He has 65 combined tackles, two sacks, and five pass breakups this year.

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

It sounds like Smith is on track to play in Week 11 against the Eagles, but it would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow or Friday. Smith also told reporters today that he was 100 percent healthy for the Eagles’ Week 6 game against the Panthers, but he managed to strain his hamstring again anyway. If active, he will be a WR2 with six teams on bye, catching passes from Joe Milton.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Donatyvion Wicks (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters he feels “pretty good” about Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) returning this week. Unfortunately for both wideouts, they will rejoin an offense now led by Joe Milton. With Smith commanding a massive target share and Makai Lemon in the mix for opportunities, Wicks will be relegated to the WR5 ranks if he suits up this week.

item.title: Will Shipley (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

Shipley was designated to return from injured reserve on Monday. He can be officially activated at any time. Shipley will reclaim his RB2 role once healthy, though we don’t expect much fantasy value to come of it.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley is no longer listed with a back injury, and is practicing in full post-bye. Both factors are extremely encouraging. The veteran running back is an RB1 against the Steelers this week, likely with an uptick in touches compared to the 13-carry workload he handled in Week 9 against the Giants.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Nick Herbig (ribs/hip) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Nick Herbig PIT Linebacker

Herbig hobbled off the field in the Steelers’ Week 10, Monday Night Football game against the Bengals. Patrick Queen (hand) was limited today, and the Steelers designated Gennings Dunker (knee) to return from injured reserve. He is practicing fully this week.

Source: Brooke Pryor

item.title: Ravens activated Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Adam Randall BAL Running Back

Randall is practicing in full and should be good to go for Week 11. He is set to make his NFL debut against the Panthers. With Derrick Henry hogging most of the carries and Justice Hill handling the passing downs, Randall will likely be limited to special teams for now.

item.title: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Omarion Hampton has reestablished himself as the team’s lead running back.
item.description:
Omarion Hampton LAC Running Back

The Athletic’s Noah Furtado asked Harbaugh why it took Hampton so long to reestablish himself as the team’s top running back. Harbaugh said, “he’s there (now). He’s showing it, proving it. And that’s all. That’s what’s important to me.” Hampton totaled 22 carries and one catch in Week 10. It sounds like he has a chance to continue handling a high-volume workload in the coming weeks, though the game script could hurt him if he fails to increase his passing game usage.

Source: Noah Furtado

item.title: Jauan Jennings (calf) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Jauan Jennings MIN Wide Receiver

Jennings missed the past two games with the calf injury. A full practice today puts him on track to return for a revenge game against the 49ers. Jordan Addison is sidelined with a thumb injury, meaning Jennings will likely return to the No. 2 receiver role. He is worth a look in deeper formats, though he’s still a high-risk WR5 for Week 11.

item.title: T.J. Hockenson (wrist) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

Hockenson missed Week 10 with the wrist issue. He was also dealing with a chest injury, though the team didn’t bother listing that today. Hockenson will be reunited with Kirk Cousins on Sunday, and the Vikings will be without Jordan Addison. That could free up a few extra targets for the tight end. If healthy, Hockenson will be in the TE2 streaming conversation.

item.title: Isaiah Williams (ribs) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Isaiah Williams NYJ Wide Receiver

Williams would not normally be a name to monitor, but he tallied seven targets in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to Buffalo. Williams was forced to take on more work after Omar Cooper Jr. went down with an ankle injury. We suspect the Jets would lean on their 12-personnel alignment if Williams and Cooper are out for Week 11. That would finally get first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq on the field more.

item.title: Taliese Fuaga (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Taliese Fuaga NO Tackle

Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, and backup OT Asim Richards (knee) were both sidelined today. Saints C Erik McCoy (biceps) is sidelined as well, though he was already expected to miss time. Hopefully, Fuaga can return in time to face the Bears this weekend. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is practicing in full.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is practicing on Wednesday.
item.description:
Talanoa Hufanga DEN Safety

Hufanga nearly played pre-bye in Week 9 against the Panthers, but he was unable to do so. He has been sidelined since injuring his ankle in Week 5 against the Chargers. Broncos S Brandon Jones (hamstring) and CB Riley Moss (concussion) are also practicing. Check back on Friday for their official statuses.

Source: Mike Klis

item.title: Caleb Douglas (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

Douglas is a little banged up coming out of Week 10, but a limited practice means he’s still on track to suit up this week. Douglas caught three of his eight targets for 71 yards last week. He has hit 70 yards in three of his past four appearances. Barring a setback, Douglas will be a boom/bust WR3 for Week 11.

item.title: Jordyn Tyson (chest) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

Saints coach Kellen Moore told reporters that Tyson suffered the chest injury in Week 10 against the Panthers. The fact that he is limited is a great sign for his availability against the Bears. Tyson belongs in fantasy football lineups on a weekly basis at this point.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Christian Benford (groin) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Christian Benford BUF Cornerback

Benford is the Bills’ No. 1 perimeter cornerback. Bills slot CB Dee Alford (concussion) and LB Dorian Williams (calf) were also sidelined to begin Week 11. The Bills face the Dolphins this weekend. Bills C Connor McGovern (neck) is practicing in full.

Source: Lance Lysowski

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers has been playing through the ankle issue for a few weeks. We expect the same for Week 11, though he hasn’t been a strong fantasy option at any point this year, healthy or not. He will remain in the WR4 ranks when the Jags take on the Giants on Sunday.

item.title: Lions activated S Kerby Joseph (knee) from the reserve/PUP list.
item.description:
Kerby Joseph DET Safety

Joseph was designated to return from the PUP list exactly three weeks ago, so they had to activate him today. He got in a full practice last week but did not travel to Germany with the team. Practicing in full once again, Joseph looks likely to make his 2026 debut in Week 11.

item.title: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Last Monday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters that Ferguson would likely miss “multiple weeks.” We do not expect him to play in Week 11 against the Titans. Check back on Friday for an official update.

Source: Nick Harris

item.title: Joey Porter (ankle/foot) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Titans.
item.description:
Joey Porter DAL Cornerback

Fellow starting CB DaRon Bland will miss time with injuries in both ankles, but at least Porter’s health is trending upward. Cowboys OLB Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle), OG Tyler Booker (ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.

Source: Nick Harris

item.title: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Skattebo returned to action last week after missing one game with the hamstring injury. He ran for 78 yards and scored twice while adding 44 yards on three grabs. Whether they want to or not, the Giants are treating Skattebo like a workhorse back once again. He is pushing to the top of the RB2 ranks heading into his Week 11 matchup with Jacksonville.

item.title: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said DaRon Bland (ankle) will “miss some time.”
item.description:
DaRon Bland DAL Cornerback

Bland entered the Cowboys’ Week 10 game against the 49ers with a left ankle injury. Unfortunately, he suffered a high-ankle sprain in his right ankle mid-game and could miss “the bulk” of the remaining schedule. Bland’s absence will make this weak defense even weaker.

Source: Dallas Cowboys

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Tuten has been playing through the pair of injuries for the past two weeks. He was held out of practice on Wednesday and Thursday last week, so a limited session today is a notable improvement. Coming off a 29-touch outing, Tuten is flirting with an RB1 ranking heading into his Week 11 matchup with the Giants.

item.title: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

Rodriguez has been playing through the hand issue for a few weeks. This time should be no different. Coming off a four-carry outing in a blowout win over the Titans, Rodriguez is tumbling into the RB4 ranks for Week 11 against the Giants.

item.title: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Kyler Gordon CHI Defensive Back

Gordon missed time earlier this season with a calf issue. He played in Week 9 before the team’s bye but got banged up. Head coach Ben Johnson called him day-to-day earlier this week. Gordon has four sacks, two forced fumbles, and one pass breakup this year. Losing him would make this an easier matchup for Tyler Shough and the Saints.

item.title: Kyle Monangai (toe) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Saints.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

Monangai has been out since Week 4 because of the toe issue. He returned to practice late last week but wasn’t ready to suit up after just one session. A full practice today all but guarantee he will be on the field this week. Monangai was splitting work with D’Andre Swift before suffering the toe injury. We suspect his role will be scaled back in his return to action, keeping him in the RB3 ranks despite the good matchup.

item.title: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back
